About the role
You'll join Chime's Growth Product Marketing team as the embedded growth owner for key parts of the consumer member funnel. You'll sit at the intersection of growth strategy, experimentation, performance analysis and product marketing craft: finding opportunities, running experiments and moving metrics against clear goals. You'll keep the core product marketing strengths of research, positioning and messaging, and go further by owning results and tradeoffs. Your work directly shapes how people find, join and start banking with Chime.
In this role, you can expect to
• You'll own growth strategy and outcomes for your part of the member funnel, from problem definition and opportunity sizing through roadmap delivery against quarterly and annual goals.
• You'll be the embedded growth marketing lead in your squads, co-owning quarterly planning and roadmaps with Product, Engineering and Analytics.
• You'll drive performance across acquisition, conversion, activation and early retention, with deep ownership of landing pages, enrollment flows and in-product onboarding.
• You'll own the growth experimentation roadmap: set clear hypotheses and success criteria, then decide what to scale, iterate or sunset based on results.
• You'll lead creative and messaging for experiments and launches across paid, lifecycle and owned surfaces, balancing speed, quality and compliance.
• You'll own incentives, promotions and offers that drive qualified acquisition of primary banking relationships, balancing CAC, activation quality and long-term value, and partner with Lifecycle so acquisition, onboarding and retention feel like one journey.
• You'll lead end-to-end GTM for your initiatives, track pacing against goals, and turn results into clear briefs and recommendations for Growth Marketing leadership.
To thrive in this role, you have
• Deep experience in growth marketing, product marketing, performance marketing or a related role, including owning a funnel metric end to end and moving it.
• A track record of driving measurable growth through experimentation and optimization, and the judgment to know when small optimizations have hit their limit and a bigger bet is needed.
• Strong analytical skills: you define success metrics, diagnose funnel performance and pull out insights that change what the team does next.
• Experience leading growth work through influence in a cross-functional squad, partnering closely with Product, Engineering and Analytics.
• Sharp positioning and messaging craft, with examples of messaging changes that materially improved performance.
• Clear storytelling and executive communication: you turn data into recommendations that leaders trust and act on.
• Bonus: consumer fintech or other regulated-industry experience; familiarity with tools like Looker, Braze and web experimentation platforms.

A little about us
At Chime, we believe that everyone can achieve financial progress. We created Chime—a financial technology company, not a bank*—on the premise that core banking services should be helpful, easy, and free. Through our user-friendly tools and intuitive platforms, we empower our members to take control of their finances and work towards their goals. Whether it's starting a savings account, purchasing a first car or home, launching a business, or pursuing higher education, we're proud to have helped millions unlock their financial potential.
We're a team of problem solvers, dreamers, and builders with one shared obsession: our members. From day one, Chimers have worked tirelessly to out-hustle and out-execute competitors to bring our mission to life. Their grit and determination inspire us to work harder every day to deliver the very best experience possible. We each bring an owner's mindset to our work, refusing to be outdone and holding ourselves accountable to meet and exceed the highest bars for our teams, our company, and our members.
We believe in being bold, dreaming big, and taking risks, while also working together, embracing our diverse perspectives, and giving each other honest feedback. Our culture remains deeply entrepreneurial, encouraging every Chimer to see themselves as stewards of our mission to help everyday Americans unlock their financial progress.
We know that to achieve our mission, we must earn and keep people's trust—so we hold ourselves to the highest standards of integrity in everything we do. These aren't just words on a wall—our values are embedded in every aspect of our business, serving as a north star that guides us as we work to help millions achieve their financial potential.
Because if we don't—who will?
*Chime is a financial technology company, not a bank. Banking services provided by The Bancorp Bank, N.A. or Stride Bank, N.A., Members FDIC.

• 🏢 Our in-office work policy is designed to keep you connected - with four days a week in the office and Fridays from home for those near one of our offices, plus team and company-wide events depending on location.
• 💻 Benefits that support your work and life, including backup child, elder, and pet care and subsidized commuter benefits for eligible employees.
• ✨ Comprehensive health, financial, and wellbeing benefits designed to support you at every stage of life.

• 🫂 1% of your time off to support local community organizations of your choice

That’s why we specifically look for individuals of varying strengths, skills, backgrounds, and ideas to join our team. We believe this gives us a competitive advantage to better serve our members and helps us all grow as Chimers and individuals.

About the Role
We’re seeking a Strategic Finance Manager to join the Strategic Finance team at Chime! Chime’s StratFin team helps leaders make better decisions about how to best use Chime’s resources to build a profitable, high-growth business that’s loved by our members nationwide.
In this role, you’ll lead high-impact, high visibility workstreams across financial strategy, bank strategy & partnerships, and new product expansion. You’ll serve as a trusted finance partner to our Banking Strategy team and collaborate with leaders across Product, Risk, Legal, Analytics, and Accounting. From evaluating partner economics and commercial terms to shaping new product opportunities, you’ll bring financial rigor and sound judgment to decisions with meaningful strategic, operational, and financial trade-offs.
We’re looking for someone who can move from analysis to action: framing key business problems, developing clear recommendations, and influencing senior stakeholders and cross-functional partners towards beneficial outcomes for Chime. In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to play a key role in some of Chime’s most important decisions.
In this role, you can expect to:
• Develop economic frameworks and financial models to inform bank partnership strategy
• Partner with Chime’s Banking Strategy team to negotiate commercial agreements that balance strategic value, financial impact, risk, and operational feasibility
• Own the financial strategy and analysis for select new product development, with a focus on enabling and scaling unsecured consumer credit offerings
• Opportunistically support critical team workstreams in support of Chime-wide priorities
• Serve as a trusted Finance partner in cross-functional decision-making, helping teams navigate tradeoffs and drive strong financial outcomes
• Synthesize complex analyses into clear narratives and confidently communicate recommendations to Finance leadership and executive stakeholders
• Prioritize your work across a portfolio of projects, build trusted stakeholder relationships, and independently drive the highest-impact work forward
To thrive in this role, you bring:
• 6+ years of experience in strategic finance, investment banking, private equity, or other analytically rigorous finance roles
• Experience in fintech, financial services, consumer lending, banking, or other highly regulated industries is a plus
• Strong financial modeling and analytical skills, with experience framing ambiguous problems, testing key assumptions, using AI tooling for modeling and analysis, and translating model output into actionable recommendations
• Experience evaluating commercial agreements, developing partner-facing negotiation strategies, and achieving favorable negotiated outcomes
• Excellent communication skills, with the ability to influence senior executives
• A proven track record of owning workstreams end-to-end, collaborating effectively across teams, and delivering business outcomes
• A low-ego, roll-up-your-sleeves approach, a willingness to operate at both the strategic and tactical levels, and the ability to handle tight deadlines and a fast-moving team culture

At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.
About the Finance team
The Finance team ensures Affirm remains financially sound and strategically positioned for growth. Our team manages financial planning, accounting, pricing, vendor management, tax, investor relations, and corporate development. We deliver timely insights, accurate reporting, and careful analysis to support decision-making. From day-to-day financial operations to major investments, we enable sustainable, informed growth by maintaining strong fiscal discipline.
About the role
We are looking for a self-motivated, hardworking, and analytically minded professional to join the Strategic Finance team during a pivotal moment of growth! As Affirm Bank is currently in its formation phase, we are actively building out our foundational team. Reporting to the Bank Head of Strategic Finance, the Bank Strategic Finance Lead will play a key role in the formation and operational build-out of the Bank. You will develop and monitor Bank financial and KPI forecasts, drive strategy, and perform financial analyses throughout the Bank. Your work will help set Bank-level goals, annual budgets, capital stress testing and monitoring, and stakeholder guidance, while building the infrastructure to hold the Bank accountable to achieving its goals. You will have a unique opportunity to work cross-functionally and use quantitative insights to drive better decision-making across the organization. The ideal candidate will not only have superb technical skills but also strong interpersonal skills and the ability to influence cross-functionally and present to all levels of the Bank organization.
What you’ll do
• Develop the end-to-end forecasting and budget process, and design, build, and maintain complex financial models to support strategic planning, scenario analysis, and decision-making
• Drive business outcomes and performance management by developing automated financial analytics dashboards and reporting infrastructure
• Analyze, diagnose variances, and report realized financial performance to Bank Executives, the Bank CFO, and other company leaders
• Develop capital stress testing, ongoing monitoring, and help establish performance measurements and targets while ensuring analytic rigor in decision-making
• Partner closely with Affirm, Inc. cross-functional teams to integrate financial workflows and join a tight-knit team with outsized impact
What we look for
• Passion and drive to build robust financial models
• Bachelor’s Degree in Business, Finance, Accounting, or related field
• 3+ years of relevant experience in analytical roles (e.g., strategic finance, consulting, data science, or analytics)
• Strong working knowledge of financial modeling tools
• Excellent proficiency in predictive analytics and forecasting
• Familiarity with fintech, lending, and payments business models preferred
• Proven ability to operate with ownership and influence in a fast-paced, dynamic, and ambiguous work environment with strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills
Base Pay Grade - K
Equity Grade - USA 6
Employees new to Affirm typically come in at the start of the pay range. Affirm focuses on providing a simple and transparent pay structure which is based on a variety of factors, including location, experience and job-related skills.
Base pay is part of a total compensation package that may include equity rewards, monthly stipends for health, wellness and tech spending, and benefits (including 100% subsidized medical coverage, dental and vision for you and your dependents.)
USA base pay range (CA, WA, NY, NJ, CT) per year: $145,000 - $205,000
USA base pay range (All other US states) per year: $128,000 - $188,000

About IT
The IT team enables Affirmers to work securely and efficiently. We manage internal devices, networks, and systems, ensuring employees can collaborate and perform at their best. Our team supports onboarding, troubleshooting, and scaling technology across locations. We focus on usability, reliability, and security to maintain a productive work environment. The IT team ensures that Affirmers have the tools and support they need—wherever they work.
About the role
As an IT Product Manager, you'll help Affirmers embrace new ways of working and get more value from the technology they use every day. Partnering with IT leadership and teams across Affirm, you'll translate employee needs into product priorities, shape technology roadmaps and lifecycle decisions, and drive adoption of collaboration, productivity, and emerging AI-powered capabilities.
What You'll Do
We are looking for a collaborative, adaptable IT Product Manager to help Affirmers work more effectively by shaping how we manage, use, and adopt collaboration, productivity, and AI-powered workplace technologies.
• You will partner with IT leadership to define and manage priorities for Affirm's collaboration and productivity tools, including Slack, Notion, Google Workspace, and emerging AI-powered technologies.
• You will turn employee needs, business priorities, and technical constraints into clear requirements, practical solutions, and actionable roadmaps that guide technology improvements.
• You will help guide the technology lifecycle, from evaluating new solutions and developing business cases to optimizing existing investments, supporting vendor renewals, and recommending when to consolidate or retire tools.
• You will lead the rollout and adoption of new tools, features, and AI-powered capabilities, partnering with Internal Communications, business leaders, and employee champions to help Affirmers navigate change with confidence.
• You will connect Affirmers with practical guidance, self-service resources, and learning opportunities—leveraging vendor expertise, existing materials, and on-demand options—to help them build confidence and get more value from workplace technology.
• You will define success measures, use employee feedback, adoption data, and support trends to evaluate outcomes, and recommend improvements that enhance the employee experience and inform technology priorities.
• You will partner with IT Engineering, Security, Legal, Procurement, and vendors to deliver solutions that balance employee needs, business value, technical feasibility, cost, and risk.
What We Look For
You bring hands-on technology experience, a product mindset, and a people-first approach to solving problems, collaborating across teams, and helping others embrace change.
• You have 5+ years of relevant experience in IT product or program management, workplace technology, technology-focussed organizational change management, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and practical experience.
• You have experience identifying and delivering improvements to employee workflows through enterprise collaboration and productivity platforms, such as Slack, Notion, Google Workspace, or similar technologies, and are eager to apply that same approach to emerging AI capabilities.
• You have experience gathering stakeholder needs, defining requirements, prioritizing opportunities, and developing actionable plans or roadmaps for technology solutions.
• You have experience leading technology rollouts, organizational change initiatives, or employee adoption programs that help people confidently embrace new tools and ways of working.
• You communicate clearly with different audiences and have experience identifying, organizing, and sharing resources that help employees understand and adopt workplace technologies.
• You use data, employee feedback, and support trends to evaluate technology adoption, measure outcomes, and identify opportunities for improvement.
• You build effective relationships across technical and business teams, using sound judgment to balance competing priorities, navigate ambiguity, and influence decisions without direct authority.

The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. The CTO organization spans 700+ people across Platform, AI, Engineering, Enterprise Engineering and IT. The Chief of Staff to the CTO is a one-person force multiplier. You own the CTO's time, attention, decisions, and follow-through, and increasingly you build the AI agents that run their operating system.
What you'll do
• Own the CTO's operating system: how their week, preparation, and decisions flow, with a running decision and commitment log so decisions get made once, stick, and each follow-up has a named owner.
• Be where they cannot be: represent them in forums and cross-functional discussions across Platform, AI, Engineering, Core, and the executive team, bring back the signal, and unblock without escalation.
• Carry their voice: write and edit town halls, AMAs, all-hands remarks, board materials, and Slack posts so their point of view lands crisply and on time.
• Build and scale AI agents that absorb more of their operating system, freeing your hours for higher-leverage work.
• Run the few things they own that have no organizational home, from framing to clean handoff, without adding process.
Required skills and experience
• 6+ years in BizOps, strategy, consulting, or technical program leadership, including support of a senior technical executive.
• Exceptional written and verbal communication: you can write in an executive's voice and turn technical trade-offs into business terms.
• Technical fluency: you follow architecture, infrastructure, and AI discussions with staff-plus engineers and ask the right questions. You do not need to be a practicing engineer.
• Judgment and discretion with sensitive org, people, and strategy information, and a clear read on what to escalate, decide, or let go.
• Influence without authority across senior engineering and cross-functional leaders, earned by being prepared and useful.
• Personal operating rigor: you track commitments and close loops relentlessly, without building process.
• Hands-on use of AI tools in your own work; experience in a platform, infrastructure, developer tooling, or AI-focused organization is a plus.
• Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality.

About Upstart
At Upstart, we’re united by a mission that matters: to radically reduce the cost and complexity of borrowing for all Americans. Every day, we bring creativity, experimentation, and advanced AI to reshape access to credit, helping millions move forward financially with clarity and confidence.
As the leading AI lending marketplace, we partner with banks and credit unions to expand access to affordable credit through technology that’s both radically intelligent and deeply human. Our platform runs over one million predictions per borrower using more than 3,000 signals, powering smarter, fairer decisions for millions of customers. But the numbers only hint at the impact. Every idea, every voice, and every contribution moves us closer to a world where credit never stands between people and their financial progress.
We’re proudly digital-first, giving most Upstarters the flexibility to do their best work from wherever they thrive, alongside teammates across 80+ cities in the US and Canada. Digital-first doesn’t mean distant. We’re intentional about in-person connection through team onsites, planning sessions, and moments that spark creativity and trust. And whether you choose to work primarily from home or collaborate in-person from one of our offices in Columbus, Austin, the Bay Area, or New York City, you’ll have the support to work in the way that works best for you.
If you’re energized by tackling meaningful problems, excited to innovate with purpose, and motivated by work that truly matters, we’d love to hear from you.
The Team:
Upstart's Secured Lending Fraud Oversight function is the Bank's first-line fraud detection, investigation, and monitoring across the HELOC and Auto Lending business lines. As a business unit function, the team owns fraud risk identification, investigation of suspected fraudulent activity, referral package preparation, and fraud trend analysis and reporting. The fraud function operates with direct access to loan files, origination data, and dealer and channel relationships — enabling the depth and speed of investigation that the Bank's fraud risk profile demands. The team works in close coordination with the Secured Lending Quality Control function: QC analysts escalate fraud indicators identified during file reviews, and fraud analysts provide fraud-focused review support during lower-volume periods, consistent with a documented cross-utilization protocol and independence safeguards.
As a Fraud Analyst, you will own day-to-day fraud detection and investigation for your assigned product line(s). You will investigate suspected fraud across the entire loan life cycle from application through loan servicing; identify and document emerging typologies and fraud patterns; prepare escalation and SAR referral packages for review; and partner with Operations, Risk, Compliance, and Legal to strengthen fraud controls across the business.
This is an opportunity for an experienced fraud professional who is energized by building investigation programs in a fast-paced, technology-driven lending environment — and who wants to operate at the intersection of fraud, compliance, and AI-powered risk controls.
How you’ll make an impact
• Own first-line fraud detection and investigation across your assigned secured lending product line(s), monitoring for suspicious activity and fraud indicators across application, origination, and servicing
• Investigate key fraud risks and emerging typologies, including application fraud, identity fraud (true-name and synthetic), income and employment misrepresentation, collateral fraud, and Auto dealer-related fraud patterns
• Investigate product specific fraud typologies including occupancy misrepresentation, valuation inflation, and undisclosed liabilities or loan stacking
• Prepare comprehensive fraud escalation and SAR referral packages for review — documenting facts, evidence, typology, and recommendations
• Conduct early payment default (EPD) fraud file reviews — performing fraud indicator review on loans reaching 60+ days past due within 90 days of origination
• Monitor and analyze fraud trends across origination channels, including application fraud rates, dealer-level fraud indicators, geographic concentrations, synthetic identity patterns, and channel-level risk signals; producing fraud metrics and trend reporting
• Maintain dealer fraud scorecards (Auto) and channel-level fraud indicator tracking, including pattern-based referrals and dealer suspension triggers in coordination with Vendor Management and dealer oversight functions
• Integrate closely with the Secured Lending QC team — triage fraud-related alerts surfaced by the QC Engine's daily monitoring output; provide typology and red flag feedback to improve detection rules and origination controls
• Coordinate across Operations, Compliance, Legal, and Risk on fraud control enhancements, law enforcement information requests, and regulatory response support
• Proactively identify regulatory risks related to fraud in your product line(s) and adjacent areas, including obligations under OCC Bulletin 2019-37, FFIEC BSA/AML Manual, Red Flags Rule (12 CFR Part 41, Subpart J), 12 CFR 21.11, and product-specific fraud risk requirements
• Support examination readiness by maintaining audit-ready fraud investigation case records, typology documentation, and program evidence aligned with OCC, FDIC, and CFPB expectations
Minimum Qualifications
• 3+ years of experience in fraud investigation, fraud analytics, or financial crimes within consumer lending, banking, or a regulated financial institution
• Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience
• Experience investigating consumer lending fraud — including application fraud, identity fraud, income/employment misrepresentation, and collateral fraud
• Experience preparing fraud investigation case documentation — fact and evidence assembly, typology analysis, and written escalation packages for compliance or legal review
• Familiarity with SAR referral processes, 12 CFR 21.11 SAR thresholds and timelines
• Working knowledge of BSA/AML program requirements applicable to consumer lending, including CIP/CDD, OFAC screening, suspicious activity monitoring, and Red Flags Rule obligations
• Working knowledge of OCC enterprise fraud risk management and FFIEC BSA/AML Manual requirements relevant to fraud investigation and suspicious activity reporting
• Experience with fraud trend analysis — application fraud rate monitoring, typology identification, channel and geographic concentration analysis
• Ability to manage own workload, meet deadlines, and proactively communicate risk to timelines with minimal supervision
• Strong cross-functional collaboration skills — able to work effectively with Operations, Compliance, Legal, and Risk on fraud escalation and control improvement initiatives
Preferred Qualifications
• Experience investigating dealer channel fraud, including power booking, ghost down payments, straw purchases, VIN cloning, title washing, and F&I product abuse
• Experience maintaining dealer-level fraud scorecards and pattern-based dealer monitoring or suspension workflows
• Experience investigating collateral fraud typologies in home equity lending — occupancy misrepresentation, appraisal inflation, undisclosed liabilities/loan stacking
• Familiarity with CIP/CDD execution requirements and fraud red flags in account draw activity and maintenance
• Experience identifying fraud indicators across income, identity, appraisal, and title documentation within origination files
• Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE) designation or active progress toward CFE certification
• Experience with fraud metrics reporting to management committees (Credit Committee, Risk Committee, or equivalent)
• Familiarity with EPD review processes and OCC fraud loss classification requirements
• Ability to translate investigation findings into structured, examination-ready documentation for OCC, FDIC, or CFPB review
• Collaborative approach to working across fraud, compliance, legal, and quality control functions in a fast-paced fintech environment

The majority of our employees can live and work anywhere in the U.S but are encouraged to to still spend high quality time in-person collaborating via regular onsites. You will partner closely with Product, Product Marketing, and our Sales & CSO teams from early product development through launch to drive in-year revenue. This means leading the Pricing & Packaging for new product launches, annual price increases, partner co-marketing initiatives, and more.

About Clear Street:
Clear Street is modernizing the brokerage ecosystem. Founded in 2018, Clear Street is a diversified financial services firm replacing the legacy infrastructure used across capital markets.
We started from scratch by building a completely cloud-native clearing and custody system designed for today’s complex, global market. Our platform is fully integrated with central clearing houses and exchanges to support billions in trading volume per day. We’ve agonized about our data model abstractions, created horizontal scalability, and crafted thoughtful APIs. All so we can provide a best-in-class experience for our clients.
By combining highly-skilled product and engineering talent with seasoned finance professionals, we’re building the essentials to compete in today’s fast-paced markets.
The Team:
You will work on a team that will own risk across Clear Street’s business lines, playing a crucial role in the success of our growing business. As a Prime Brokerage and Clearing Risk Manager specializing in options, you will contribute to creating, evolving and executing the risk frameworks and best practices that support our futures and options clearing as well as our prime brokerage clients. This is an impactful position that provides the opportunity to expand both your quantitative and client-facing skill sets. You will cover US and international listed options markets, across multi-asset portfolios.
Responsibilities:
• Serve as a primary point of contact for clients, including options market makers, hedge funds and proprietary trading firms, on portfolio onboarding, risk reviews and ongoing risk management topics.
• Monitor intraday and end-of-day risk exposures and margin requirements across client options portfolios, including exposure to delta, gamma, vega and volatility and underlying price shocks.
• Track US and international options markets through OMS, clearing and risk systems, and escalate material issues such as concentrated positions, expiration and assignment risk, and large moves in volatility to senior management as needed.
• Develop and maintain robust margin, risk and stress-testing methodologies, including options-based portfolio margin (such as TIMS, SPAN and OCC STANS), customer margin under Reg T, and clearing margin.
• Monitor and manage clearing exposures, including OCC and clearinghouse margin and clearing fund requirements, exercise and assignment, and settlement risk.
• Generate and automate ad-hoc reporting to highlight key risk factors, scenario results and portfolio exposures.
• Communicate critical risk observations to senior risk management and external clients.
• Support ongoing initiatives to develop and enhance the firm’s risk, margin and clearing platforms.
• Collaborate with internal stakeholders, including technology, operations and product teams, to improve risk management infrastructure and margin capabilities.
Requirements:
• At least five (5) years of professional experience in prime brokerage risk, clearing risk, options trading risk or related roles, either on the sell-side or buy-side, with direct exposure to listed options and equity derivatives.
• A minimum of five (5) years of overall professional experience in financial services; prior experience as a trader or a prime brokerage / prime services risk manager highly preferred.
• Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Mathematics or Financial Engineering required; Master’s degree preferred.
• Strong understanding of options pricing and risk measures (the Greeks, implied volatility, skew and term structure), complex multi-leg strategies, and equity and index products.
• Proficiency in Python and SQL preferred.
• Familiarity with industry-standard tools such as Bloomberg, ICE and FactSet, and with options risk and clearing platforms.
• Working knowledge of the regulatory frameworks, capital and margin rules for options and clearing, including Reg T, portfolio margin, SEC Rule 15c3-1 and 15c3-3, and OCC clearing member requirements.
•
• Strong communication skills, with the ability to engage confidently with clients and regulators.
• Proactive, collaborative and a strong team player with a high sense of ownership.
• Demonstrated project management experience and the ability to work closely with engineering and cross-functional teams.
• Analytical and detail-oriented, with strong quantitative aptitude.
• Experience in risk policy development and implementation.

About the role:
Forter is looking for a passionate, technically-grounded Senior Solutions Consultant. This is a market-building role as much as it is a technical sales role: you'll be one of the technical tips of the spear as Forter enters and scales in new markets, responsible not only for winning individual deals but for capturing the market intelligence that tells us where and how to win. As a trusted advisor to our sales organization and a key voice into Product, Risk, Engineering, Marketing, and CS, Solutions Consultants ensure our growth is grounded in strong technical alignment between Forter's AI-powered trust platform and the complex, evolving needs of the world's largest, fastest-growing digital businesses.
Forter Solutions Consultants guide prospects and customers through the technical evaluation of our platform, translating deep AI/ML domain expertise into clear business outcomes. In emerging markets specifically, you'll also own the feedback loop that turns field experience into a sharpened go-to-market strategy: surfacing what you're seeing on the ground, forming a point of view on where to prioritize, and helping the business run rapid, repeatable experiments toward revenue outcomes.
We are looking to speak with candidates who bring a strong technical sales background, deep AI/ML fluency, and the presence to operate credibly with both technical and business leadership at large, complex organizations, including in markets where the playbook isn't written yet.
What you’ll be doing:
In this role, you will work on complex, high-stakes opportunities where analysis of a prospect's data, models, and architecture requires deep technical evaluation, and where your on-the-ground observations directly shape how Forter approaches an entire market. You will:
•
• Technical Discovery & Solution Design: Lead technical discovery with prospects' data science, engineering, and risk teams to understand their existing models, data infrastructure, and decisioning logic, and design how Forter's platform integrates with and improves upon them
• AI/ML Credibility & Value Translation: Engage as a domain-credible peer to prospects' AI/ML and data teams, then translate that technical depth into a clear, quantified business impact narrative for executive and business stakeholders
• Market Data Capture & GTM Intelligence: Systematically capture market and technical discovery data across your Emerging Markets deals (buyer maturity, competitive landscape, technical objections, regulatory nuance, integration patterns) and turn it into an honed point of view on GTM prioritization and feasibility for internal teams
• Sales Partnership: Partner with Sales Executives to drive account strategy, opportunity qualification, and pipeline generation, owning all technical aspects of the sales cycle: discovery, demos, proof of value, RFP/security responses, and technical closing
• Executive & Business Stakeholder Engagement: Build trusted relationships across both technical (CTO/CPO org) and business-side stakeholders (Ecommerce teams, revenue business owners), positioning Forter as a strategic partner to the whole business, not just a point solution for IT
• Cross-Functional Feedback Loops: Serve as a connective layer between the field and internal teams (Product, Risk, Engineering, Marketing, and CS), surfacing prospect and market feedback quickly and repeatably, and helping design experiments that convert field learning into revenue outcomes in a repeatable way
• Customer Success Handoff: Ensure a clean, well-documented technical handoff to CS/Implementation post-sale, setting new customers up for long-term success
• Innovation and Improvement: Continuously identify opportunities to improve Forter's platform, tooling, and sales process, and mentor other members of the Solutions Consulting team
• Personal Training and Development: Stay current on evolving fraud, payments, and AI/ML landscape trends, as well as Forter's expanding product suite
What you’ll need:
•
• 8+ years of experience in a customer-facing technical role, with 5+ years specifically in pre-sales/solutions consulting, sales engineering, or a similar technical sales capacity at enterprise software companies
• A strong Data Science and/or Data Analytics background, with hands-on experience building, evaluating, or deploying AI/ML models
• Demonstrated ability to work directly with AI/ML and data science teams at prospect organizations, able to speak their language, earn technical credibility, and translate model performance and architecture into business impact for less technical stakeholders
• A track record of selling into large, highly complex organizations, ideally with experience navigating multi-stakeholder, multi-threaded enterprise sales cycles
• Preferred experience selling into the CTO/CPO organization, as well as engaging directly with business-side personas (Ecommerce teams and the revenue business owners that CTO/CPO orgs ultimately need to support), so that technical evaluation stays tied to commercial outcomes
• Comfort operating in ambiguity and building structure where none exists, with a genuine curiosity about new and emerging markets and the ability to synthesize scattered market signals into a clear, actionable point of view
• Excellent presentation, communication, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to move fluidly between deep technical conversations and executive-level business narratives
• Strong cross-functional collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across Product, Risk, Engineering, Marketing, Customer Success, and Sales to build rapid, repeatable feedback mechanisms between the field and internal teams
• The ability to travel as needed to support the emerging markets territory
• A Bachelor's degree in a technical or quantitative field (Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Engineering, or related), or equivalent work experience
• You may also have:
• Experience in fraud prevention, payments, or e-commerce risk, highly beneficial, though secondary to AI/ML modeling depth and technical sales experience
• Experience with modern data science tooling and languages (e.g. Python, SQL, R) and ML frameworks
• Familiarity with real-time decisioning systems, transaction risk scoring, or similar high-throughput, low-latency architectures
• Understanding of popular sales methodologies/frameworks such as MEDDPICC / Command of the Message
• Prior experience opening up or scaling a new market or territory for a technology company, including building GTM point of view from limited data
About Us:
Commerce is evolving faster than the systems built to support it. Agentic AI is redrawing how people buy. Customer expectations have a new ceiling. And bad actors are evolving alongside every advancement.
Forter was built to meet this moment — and stay ahead of it.
We are a human-first, AI-built company. Our technology analyzes patterns across a network of over 2 billion shoppers, delivering identity intelligence across the entire commerce journey — from sign-up to checkout to returns — that protects revenue and unlocks great customer experiences simultaneously. With Forter, businesses know who to trust, whether it’s humans or the agents shopping for them. The result: zero friction for the customers who matter. No revenue left behind.
The world's most trusted brands — Nordstrom, Instacart, Priceline, Adobe, ASOS, and eBay among them — rely on Forter to get this right. Since 2013, we've raised $525M from investors including Tiger Global, Bessemer, Sequoia Capital, and Salesforce Ventures, and today we power commerce decisions for nearly 1 million businesses globally. We're more than fraud, payments and orchestration – we make trust a competitive advantage.
Trust is backed by data – Forter is a recipient of over 10 workplace and innovation awards, including:
• Great Place to Work Certification (2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 )
• Fortune’s Best Workplaces in NYC (2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025 )
• Forbes Cloud 100 (2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025 )
• Anti-Fraud Solution of the Year at the Payments Awards ( 2024 )
Life as a Forterian:
Forterians are, genuinely, some of the best people you'll work with. Smart, curious, and deeply good humans who care about the work and each other. That's not an accident — it's something we've been intentional about since day one, and it's the thing people mention most when they talk about why they stay. When you're surrounded by people like this, doing work that actually matters, it changes what a job can feel like.
Forter was built on a simple but powerful conviction: when AI does its job, humans can do theirs better. That philosophy shapes our products and shapes how we work. AI is core to our workflows — not as a shortcut, but as a force multiplier that gives Forterians the space to focus their energy where human judgment is irreplaceable.
We're a global team of 500+ people, with regional headquarters in New York, Tel Aviv, London, and Singapore, and employee presence across the US, Canada, Germany, France, Japan, China, and Australia. Our teams are cross-functional by design, and the work you do here is visible, consequential, and connected to the outcomes that matter.
You'll have real ownership here and proximity to decisions. And we back that with investment in your growth — RSU offerings, L&D programs built around AI tools, and a culture of recognition rooted in our 4.5 day weeks (aka Forter’s Appreciation Fridays and Sundays). From team outings to local cultural celebrations, we mark the moments that matter — wherever you are in the world. We don't want Forter to be just another job. We want it to be the place you build.

About Paxos

Today’s financial infrastructure is archaic, expensive, inefficient and risky — supporting a system that leaves out more people than it lets in. So we’re rebuilding it.

We’re on a mission to open the world’s financial system to everyone by enabling the instant movement of any asset, any time, in a trustworthy way. About the team

Paxos is positioning itself as a connected platform to create, custody, distribute and utilize digital assets, and Custody is the control plane of those assets. The Custody product team owns the capabilities that let institutional customers hold, control, and move assets securely, and works hand in hand with Engineering, Compliance/Legal, Operations, and Go-To-Market teams to win tier-1 financial institutions globally.

About the role

Custody is where institutions decide whether they can trust Paxos with their assets. As Senior Product Manager, Custody, you’ll own the product that holds and secures those assets, including wallet management and the controls around how assets move, and set its direction as demand grows from crypto-native firms to banks, asset managers, and wealth platforms.

You’ll form a point of view on where institutional custody is heading and what Paxos needs to build to lead there, then drive it from strategy through launch. That means deciding where to invest to meet the security bar institutions require while staying flexible enough for how customers actually operate. You’ll work through technically deep problems with Engineering and learn directly from institutional clients what it takes for them to go live, turning their requirements into the product.

This is an individual contributor role with real ownership of a strategy that drives institutional adoption of our custody products.

What you’ll do

 - Own the Custody strategy and roadmap, and drive it through execution, from defining requirements to launch and iteration

 - Define the security and control capabilities institutional customers rely on to protect and govern their assets, including wallet management and the controls around how assets are held and moved

 - Drive the infrastructure and integrations that extend Custody to meet institutional requirements, including relationships with third-party providers and partners

 - Collaborate with Engineering, Design, Compliance, Legal, and Operations to deliver capabilities that are secure, usable, and meet the regulatory expectations of institutional clients

 - Work with Go-To-Market teams to drive adoption of new capabilities, from positioning and client onboarding to feedback that shapes what comes next

OUR MISSION:

Omnea is the agentic operating system for procurement.

Procurement touches every pound a business spends, yet requests still stall for weeks and approvals get lost in inboxes. Our AI-first platform changes that: our agents capture requests, route approvals, onboard suppliers, flag risk and track every renewal, while anyone in the business can ask a question and get an answer grounded in their own company’s data. Buying becomes painless for everyone, procurement gets a seat at the table, and our customers have saved more than 100,000 hours of manual work so far.

Companies like Spotify, PayPal, T. Rowe Price, JustEat, Adyen and S&P Global run procurement on Omnea. We’re backed by $75M from Khosla Ventures, Insight Partners and Accel, and we’ve been named the UK’s number one startup in the Startups 100, ranked 11th on Sifted’s 2026 list of Europe’s fastest-growing companies, and recognised as one of Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies.

Talent density matters more to us than almost anything else. We keep the bar high in every team, so everyone here has real ownership and real impact. Our team is full of former founders and operators who’ve scaled unicorns, and we’re looking for people who want to do the best work of their careers alongside them.



Find out more about the team and life at Omnea here https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLpjeHyocsu3ZoDn3sfODjqIR2L_DW3dgb.




THE ROLE

AI is changing what it means to deploy enterprise software. Configuring a customer's procurement workflows used to mean weeks of manual setup, integration by integration, edge case by edge case. Increasingly, that first-draft build work can be directed rather than done by hand: AI agents can generate workflow configurations, draft integration mappings, and produce the initial pass on a customer's setup.

The job shifts with it. Instead of building every workflow yourself, you specify exactly what needs to exist, direct AI to build it, and apply the judgment AI can't: is this the right configuration for this customer's approval policy, will Legal and Finance actually sign off on it, does it hold up once real spend starts flowing through it. In practice, that might mean catching that the approval chain AI just drafted works perfectly for HQ, but misses a regional delegation-of-authority rule that would fail an audit in the customer's APAC entity.

As Omnea's AI Solutions Lead, you own deployment of the Omnea platform end to end - typically running 3-5 enterprise deployments concurrently - for some of Europe's most recognisable companies. You advise customers on the best-fit configuration, direct AI-assisted build work to get there fast, and validate every output against what the customer actually needs. You'll also deal with the politics that come with every enterprise rollout: the Legal team wanting one more sign-off, the Finance stakeholder who doesn't trust the new approval flow, the exec sponsor who's gone quiet. You become the internal voice of the customer, and you're judged on outcomes you can point to: time to launch, post-go-live CSAT, and whether that customer becomes a case study or reference.

This is an early hire on Omnea's customer team, working directly with our sales, customer, product, and engineering leadership. The future shape of the role is yours to define!


WHAT YOU'LL DO


DISCOVER AND DESIGN

 - Run discovery with customer stakeholders across Procurement, Finance, Legal, and IT, and translate their process into an Omnea configuration

 - Design the target workflow: approval chains, routing logic, integrations, and the edge cases that make procurement hard

 - On a deployment with a dozen-plus integrations, you own the sequencing - what has to land first, what blocks what - and the harder calls underneath it: which system is the source of truth for a given entity, and how records reconcile when two systems key that entity differently

 - Define success criteria and a realistic path to go-live with the customer's project sponsor


BUILD WITH AI, NOT INSTEAD OF IT

 - You're not just directing AI to draft your own deliverables faster - you're configuring the specialized agents Omnea's customers rely on every day: an intake agent that knows how to ask a procurement analyst the right follow-up question, a risk agent that flags what actually matters to this customer's Legal team

 - The real leverage comes from chaining agents together - an intake agent that hands clean, structured requests to a risk agent, which in turn routes into approvals with the right context already attached. You design how those agents work as a system, not just individually

 - Writing a spec for one agent is a skill. Writing one that holds up across a chain of agents - where one agent's output becomes another's input - is the actual bar here

 - Validate every AI-generated output against the customer's actual process, policy, and edge cases before anything ships

 - Handle what AI can't: judgment calls on ambiguous requirements, custom logic, and anything that needs a human read on internal politics


DEPLOY AND PROVE VALUE

 - Present configured workflows to stakeholders, from procurement analysts to CFOs, working through the pushback and internal politics that come with any enterprise rollout, and win their buy-in

 - Run multi-day onsite workshops with customers, coordinating dozens of stakeholders across multiple workstreams at once - a different muscle than a single stakeholder meeting

 - Project-manage the deployment: timelines, blockers, stakeholder alignment, and a clear path to launch, acting as an extension of the customer's team

 - Track adoption after go-live and keep the configuration working as the customer's process evolves

 - Work with Product and Engineering during the design phase, not just after something breaks in the field - you're often the earliest signal on whether a new module will hold up for an enterprise customer, and that shapes what gets built next


WHAT'S DIFFERENT ABOUT THIS ROLE

 - You'll spend more time specifying and validating than building from scratch. AI produces the first draft; you make sure it's right for this customer

 - Writing instructions AI can act on precisely is a skill you'll build fast here. Vague requests produce vague configurations

 - Judgment matters more, not less. AI speeds up the build, but you decide whether the output is right for this contract, this Board, this customer

 - You'll keep experimenting as our AI tooling evolves, and share what works with the rest of the team


ABOUT YOU

We don't expect you to know how to do all of this on day one. TL;DR: you're ambitious and hard-working, as comfortable directing an AI agent through a tricky configuration as you are presenting a project plan to an exec. You make up for any gap in experience with hunger and a genuine growth mindset. You derive energy from building relationships, shipping projects, and making customers succeed.

 - 4-8 years in a fast-paced, high-bar environment: a startup, scale-up, consulting, banking, or something you built yourself

 - Comfortable directing AI tools to produce first-draft work, and confident enough in your own judgment to catch what's wrong. Prior use of tools like ChatGPT, Claude, or Cursor is a strong plus. What matters most is your ability to write clear, specific instructions and evaluate what comes back

 - Client-facing experience, or the natural gravitas to be excellent at it. You can point to a time you went well beyond what a client expected

 - A track record of doing something exceptionally well, whether that's work, academia, sport, or anything else you've put your mind to

 - Comfortable reasoning about system architecture - how data models, primary keys, and integration sequencing interact across a dozen enterprise systems. You don't need to write the integration code, but you need to know why it breaks and be able to reason with the people who do, and you'll need to become an Omnea product expert

 - Choose our strategic partners. Land one or two in North America, and work with the VP, Partnerships to pick the partner Omnea builds its global programme around.

 - Work live deals. Bring partners into US deals and bring US deals to partners, concentrating what you route on your strategic few.

 - Run each strategic partner like an account. A joint plan and a quarterly review with the partner who owns the P&L.

 - Be the voice of the US consulting market inside Omnea. What partners tell you shapes our roadmap and our US go-to-market plan.

In your first 90 days, you've chosen your priority firms and partner-influenced deals are moving through the US pipeline.

In three years, the most influential procurement advisors in North America bring Omnea into transformations by default without being asked, driving $00Ms revenue.




YOU ARE

 - Fluent in how consultancies make money. You've worked inside one, or alongside them closely enough to understand partner economics and why a Senior Partner puts their name behind a platform.

 - At your best in the room. You build senior relationships in person cold start, at a firm that had no reason to take your call.. You're as comfortable hosting a dinner for six Senior Partners as presenting to fifty Associates.

 - Owner of a number. You've carried revenue or pipeline through partners and can show what you delivered.

At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.
At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.
Available Locations: London, New York City, Denver, Lisbon, Seattle, or Austin
About the Role
Millions of websites, applications, APIs, and AI agents run on Cloudflare, and the traffic we handle for them produces a lot of data. Some customers want to debug applications and investigate security events in Cloudflare. Others want that data in a stack they already trust, such as Splunk, Datadog, Grafana, or their own data lake. Many want both.
We're hiring one Senior Product Manager for each of two areas. You apply once, and we'll work out together which role fits you best.
Observability Platform brings logs, traces, analytics, alerts, and dashboards together in one place, so customers can see what's happening and why. Today most observability ends with a notification, and the customer does the rest. We want a platform that understands the problem, takes action where it can, and asks before doing anything risky.
Telemetry Export delivers Cloudflare's data to the tools customers choose. Logpush handles most of that delivery today, and Workers Observability sends logs and traces over the OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP). Customers want OTLP for the rest of Cloudflare's data, metrics pushed to their own tools, and a way to send us telemetry from workloads that run elsewhere.
Your mission is to make reliability and security something customers rarely have to worry about, with the data they need in Cloudflare or in the tools they already use.
What You'll Do
• Talk with customers every day and deeply understand their needs. They include developers building on Cloudflare, security teams who feed our logs into a SIEM, and platform teams who run OpenTelemetry pipelines.
• Own the strategy, roadmap, and execution for your area, and make hard trade-offs between speed, retention, reliability, and cost.
• Build on open standards like OpenTelemetry, W3C Trace Context, and SQL so teams can keep using the tools they already have.
• Own the business, including pricing, packaging, and revenue. Measure progress by adoption and reliability.
In Observability Platform , you'll also:
• Bring every Cloudflare product into one observability experience, so customers can follow a problem from one product to the next without switching tools.
• Move beyond notifications to workflows that investigate, roll back, or fix problems, with guardrails customers control.
• Give people and their agents the context they need to act safely, including how services connect and depend on each other.
• Own the experience end to end, from first setup to the middle of an incident or an audit.
In Telemetry Export , you'll also:
• Bring Logpush, Workers Logpush, and the OpenTelemetry destinations in Workers Observability together as one product, and keep existing integrations working.
• Ship metrics export and extend OTLP delivery to more of our datasets. Own the intake path for telemetry from outside Cloudflare; Observability Platform will store and query it.
• Make delivery something customers can trust, so they can see whether their data arrived, get a useful alert when it didn't, and know how to recover.
• Help customers filter and transform data before it's sent, so they export only what they need.
Who You Are
• You've shipped products people depend on, as a PM, engineer, engineering manager, SRE, or founder, and you can point to what changed because of your work.
• You move fast and own outcomes. You find the most important problem, get the team behind it, ship, and measure.
• You are a builder at heart. You love getting to a deep understanding of customer needs, and shipping things that help them accomplish their goals. You are passionate about the Observability industry and want to be on the forefront of innovating what it can turn into.
• You understand how telemetry systems fail, whether that's a delivery pipeline under backpressure or a query that scans far more data than it needs, and you can explain the reliability and cost trade-offs to engineers and to customers.
• AI is already central to how you work. You use it to prototype ideas and dig through data, and you have a view on how agents will produce telemetry and act on it.
Examples of Desirable Skills, Knowledge, and Experience
• You've relied on observability yourself, on call during an outage or in a security investigation, and you know where today's tools fall short.
• You've run or built on telemetry pipelines such as the OpenTelemetry Collector, Vector, Fluent Bit, or Kafka, or you've ingested someone else's data at scale at a vendor.
• You notice friction, like a confusing error message or a query that takes too many steps, and you fix it.
• You've priced a usage-based product, and you know what happens when existing customers start paying for something that used to be included.
• You're comfortable with enterprise customers, whether you're talking about compliance with a security team or OTLP with a platform engineer.
• You write clearly enough to get teams across Cloudflare to agree on a plan, and you can translate between what customers need and what engineering builds.

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.
Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.
About the role:
Samsara’s Mid-Market Customer Success team advises and guides our customers, ensuring they adopt Samsara and continuously gain business value from our products. We are the trusted point of contact for Samsara’s Mid-Market customers throughout their lifecycle: onboarding, adoption, advocacy, and renewal.
In this role, you will be part of our Implementation team, responsible for helping Mid-Market customers deploy and adopt our IoT solutions for their fleet and industrial assets. Picking up where our sales teams leave off, you will own the customer relationship and ensure a successful deployment of Samsara's solution. Your customers span the entire range of businesses that power our economy, including trucking and transportation, food and beverage, passenger transit, utilities, school buses, and many others. All the while building relationships with the customer, helping them learn our system, establishing success metrics for business outcomes and overall ensuring a successful customer relationship.
Your role will be cross-functional in nature, working alongside and connecting Sales, Support, Sales Engineering, and Product, enabling you to experience multiple aspects of a fast-growing company from within.
This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area.
You should apply if:
• You want to impact the industries that run our world: Every phone call you answer and every email you send can affect whether truck drivers deliver goods on time and without accidents, whether students get dropped off safely from school, or whether power gets restored quickly after a natural disaster.
• You thrive the most when solving problems: Our constantly expanding technology and the complexities faced by our customers provide an exciting range of challenges for our Customer Success teams. With a growth mindset and a desire to learn, you will strategically partner with our customers to find unique solutions to help keep their operations safe, efficient, and sustainable.

• Deeply understand the Samsara platform’s capabilities, explain them to customers of all types, and measure success of desired business outcomes

• Excellent consultative skills with experience in end-to-end system implementations
• Proven track record of building trust and communicating effectively with a wide variety of stakeholders: executives, Product and Engineering leadership, day-to-day users of our software
• Experience defining business outcomes, measuring success through clear metrics and KPIs, and establishing ROI
• Diplomacy, tact, and poise under pressure when working through customer issues

ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI’s Integrity team protects people and businesses using ChatGPT, Codex, and the API from fraud, abuse, and harmful misuse. Our work spans payment and promotional abuse, compromised accounts and API credentials, business and advertiser integrity, and emerging misuse of frontier AI capabilities. We also help product teams measure authentic usage so that abuse doesn’t distort decisions about how our products are growing.

Integrity Data Science helps teams decide where to intervene and whether those interventions work. A payment control can prevent fraud while blocking legitimate purchases. A product launch can make it easier for customers to get started while creating new opportunities for abuse. We measure both sides of those decisions.



ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Data Scientist on Integrity, you’ll find emerging abuse patterns, size their impact, and lead the analytical work behind decisions about detection, enforcement, and product launches. You’ll work with Product, Engineering, Research, Policy, and Operations to turn findings into improvements and measure what happens after they ship.

 - Investigate anomalous activity across products. Estimate how common a problem is, who is affected, and what it costs users or the business. Use that evidence to recommend where to focus.

 - Define outcome metrics and guardrails, establish baselines, and build monitoring that surfaces changes in abuse, customer friction, and operational performance.

 - Help build and evaluate detection rules, classifiers, and human review workflows. Use labeled samples and review outcomes to understand what the systems miss, where they flag legitimate activity, and how those errors vary across users and products.

 - Design randomized holdouts and use quasi-experimental or observational methods when randomization is impractical. Estimate harm or fraud losses prevented alongside effects on legitimate users, revenue, compute costs, and review workload. Recommend whether to launch, expand, adjust, or retire a control.

 - Trace where signals, review decisions, or enforcement actions break down. Work with partners to close gaps and build reusable datasets, analyses, and investigation tools.



IDEAL CANDIDATE

 - You use AI tools to investigate large, messy datasets, test hypotheses quickly, and automate recurring analyses. You’re fluent in SQL and Python and can verify AI-generated queries, code, and conclusions against the underlying data.

 - You have strong statistical judgment and experience with experimentation, causal inference, or observational analysis. You can reason from incomplete or biased labels and explain how uncertainty affects a decision.

 - You take ownership of open-ended problems, from deciding what to measure through recommending an action and checking whether it worked.

 - You communicate clearly with technical and nontechnical partners and can explain the tradeoffs behind a recommendation.

 - Experience in integrity, trust and safety, fraud or risk analytics, security analytics, or applied ML evaluation is helpful. Experience evaluating detection systems, human review, or LLM-based classifiers is a plus.

About the Team

The Frontier Risks Safety team sets out safety requirements and executes planning for frontier model launches, including biological and cyber risks and government models. We work across research, engineering, and policy to assess risks, define and validate safeguards, and drive safety readiness throughout the model development and deployment process.  We also help shape frontier trusted-access programs, ensuring that access to advanced capabilities is supported by appropriate safeguards, clear requirements, and rigorous evaluation.

 

About the Role

As a Product Manager on the Frontier Risks Safety team, you will own product strategy, requirements, and delivery for initiatives that mitigate frontier AI risks and enable responsible access to advanced capabilities.  

You will partner with researchers, engineers, policy teams, and independent experts to identify the most important problems to solve, translate research and risk assessments into product requirements, and prioritize what to build.  You will guide work from discovery through deployment and iteration, making tradeoffs explicit and measuring whether the resulting safeguards and workflows address the risks they are intended to mitigate.

We’re looking for people who combine strong technical judgment, experience building and shipping complex technical products, and a commitment to AI safety. You should be comfortable working through uncertainty, engaging deeply with research, and adapting direction as capabilities, evidence, and user needs evolve.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

 

In this role, you will:

 - Set product strategy and priorities. Develop a shared understanding of frontier risks, deployment needs, and gaps in safeguards. Own the roadmap for mitigations, prioritizing investments based on risk, evidence, technical feasibility, and the value the underlying capabilities enable for users.

 - Drive frontier trusted-access programs. Ensure defenders and scientists have access to the frontier capabilities they need to strengthen security and accelerate scientific discovery.

 - Turn safety needs into product requirements. Work with model teams, safety researchers, engineers, and policy partners to translate threat models, evaluation findings, and user needs into clear requirements, acceptance criteria, and measurable outcomes.

 - Drive safeguards from concept to deployment. Partner with research and engineering teams to turn promising safety approaches into effective mitigations across models and products.  Resolve product and technical tradeoffs, manage dependencies, and drive delivery of improvements that close material safety gaps.

 - Own risk-area safety readiness. Own risk assessments and safeguard plans for launches in your area.  Define the requirements and evidence needed for readiness reviews with technical partners, surface unresolved risks early, and bring clear recommendations to accountable safety and deployment decision-makers.

 - Use evaluations to guide product decisions. Partner with researchers to prioritize capability evals, alignment and control assessments, adversarial testing, and safeguard stress-testing, including for autonomous and multi-agent systems.  Assess what the evidence establishes, where uncertainty remains, and how findings should change the roadmap.

 - Align teams and communicate decisions. Build alignment across research, engineering, product, and policy on goals, priorities, and tradeoffs.  Resolve blockers, establish clear ownership, and communicate results, limitations, and remaining risks through decision documents, launch reviews, and contributions to system cards and assessment reports.

 

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have 5+ years of product management experience, or equivalent experience owning the direction and delivery of complex technical products.

 - Have defined and shipped products or systems with researchers and engineers, particularly in AI, cybersecurity, biosafety, or another field where failures can have serious consequences.

 - Can turn ambiguous risks and user needs into a clear product strategy, prioritized roadmap, actionable requirements, and measurable outcomes.

 - Understand frontier AI safety concepts, including capability evals, alignment, control, monitoring, and safeguard robustness, and can engage substantively with technical teams.

 - Can assess what eval results do and do not establish, including methodological limitations, uncertainty, and the difference between model capability and real-world risk.

 - Exercise sound judgment when evidence is concerning or incomplete, make practical tradeoffs, and escalate unresolved risks constructively.

 - Have worked extensively across research, engineering, and product teams and can build alignment with policy and communications partners.

 - Communicate complex technical work and product decisions clearly, including disagreement, negative results, and remaining uncertainty.

We're looking for an Applied AI Architect to join Beneficial Deployments, focused on helping nonprofits and foundations get real value from Claude. You'll be the technical lead for a portfolio of partners, working alongside our Account Executives from first conversation through deployment. You'll help partners find where Claude makes a real difference to their mission and their operations, design solutions that fit their budgets, data and teams, and turn early pilots into lasting adoption. What works for one partner becomes something the whole sector can use.

•
Serve as the primary technical advisor to a portfolio of nonprofit partners from discovery through deployment, turning their priorities into scoped use cases with clear measures of success.

Partner with Account Executives on account plans, discovery and technical evaluation.

Design and demo solutions with Claude, the API and Claude Code across program delivery, fundraising, operations and data analysis.

Run workshops and trainings that build AI fluency across partner teams.

About the role
As an Applied AI Engineer on the Commercial team at Anthropic, you will be a trusted technical advisor to the companies that run the real economy, across software, financial services, healthcare, retail, manufacturing, and professional services, as they go from using Claude to building on it. Commercial is one of Anthropic's largest and fastest-moving books of business, covering thousands of mid-market and small companies. Some of these companies put Claude inside the product they sell, and others put agents to work inside their own engineering, operations, finance, and support teams, and this role works with both. You'll lead deep technical engagements, partnering directly with customer engineering teams to take their hardest agent builds from idea to production on the Claude API, the Agent SDK, Claude Managed Agents, Claude Code, and Claude for Enterprise. Many of these teams are lean, with years of existing systems and no dedicated AI function, and you will bridge the gap between what Claude can do and what it takes to run it inside a business that already has customers depending on it.
Working closely with Applied AI Architects, Account Executives, and Anthropic's Product, Engineering, and Research teams, you'll go deep where hands-on engineering changes the outcome, then turn what you learn into something the rest of the book can use. You'll leverage your AI engineering expertise to develop custom evaluation frameworks, design scalable architectures, and create the reference implementations, tooling, and technical resources that enable Commercial customers to succeed with Claude.
Responsibilities
• Serve as a deep technical advisor to high-potential Commercial customers, whether Claude sits inside the product they sell or inside the way they run their own business, bringing them use cases worth building and pushing the boundaries of what agents can do in engineering, operations, finance, customer support, and more
• Work hands-on with customer engineering teams through build sprints, pair programming, and architecture reviews that move agents from idea to production, and understand their stack, data, and workflows end to end so that your guidance fits the systems, security requirements, and team they have today
• Ship working code. Develop prototypes, near-production examples, and technical documentation, including evaluation suites that become the customer's acceptance criteria, AI engineering techniques, and architecture diagrams, that enable customers to build, operate, and scale with Claude
• Create reference implementations, blueprints, and sample code that many companies can adopt without starting from scratch, for example multi-agent systems on the Agent SDK or Claude Managed Agents, MCP servers for common business systems, or Claude Code running across the software development lifecycle
• Collaborate closely with Applied AI Architects and Account Executives to decide where engineering depth changes the outcome, and to maintain context and continuity across customer engagements
• Identify patterns across engagements, including what is hard about running agents inside established companies such as legacy systems, messy data, permissions and security review, cost and latency at scale, and model migrations, then build repeatable evaluations and solutions and contribute insights back to Product, Engineering, Research, and the broader Applied AI team
• Build the demos, agents, and internal tooling that scale the Commercial Applied AI team itself, and pair with architects on their hardest technical problems
• Create technical content for customer and partner engineering audiences including documentation, tutorials, and sample code
• Foster community engagement through hackathons, webinars, technical office hours, and customer events
• Travel to customer sites for workshops, implementation guidance, and relationship building

• Deep software engineering experience, gained by designing, building, and operating production systems, along with strong opinions of your own about how to bridge the gap between what AI can do today and how established companies get work done
• 4+ years of technical experience as a software engineer, forward deployed engineer, ML engineer, product engineer, or technical founder, with production experience building LLM-powered applications, including prompting, context engineering, agent architectures, MCP, evaluation frameworks, and deployment at scale, and the ability to work in a real codebase in Python or TypeScript, not just notebooks
• A systems mindset and comfort with ambiguity. You'd rather build one thing that serves ten customers than ten things that serve one each, and you have a track record of building structure where the playbook doesn't exist yet
• Strong technical communication skills, with the presence to earn the trust of a customer's engineering leaders, the ability to translate complex AI concepts into architectural decisions and actionable implementation plans for both technical and business audiences, and the ability to run technical workshops, hackathons, or developer-focused events
• A collaborative approach to working across teams, the range of a generalist who can context-switch from a fintech to a hospital network to a manufacturer and get up to speed on a new business quickly, and a passion for making powerful technology safe and beneficial
