That starts with understanding the plan: how coverage, territories and account data fit together, what assumptions sit underneath them, and what happens downstream when one changes. From there you'll plan your area during the cycle, run it through the year as the business moves, and build the tools that make it easier. When something keeps breaking, we expect you to find out why and fix it at the source.
Key responsibilities
• Build and maintain the territory models and methods behind the plan
• Partner on segmentation definitions and strategy, and turn them into the account rules and criteria that territories are built on
• Carry territories from design through validation with the business, QA and go-live
• Own data enrichment and system requirements for territories and accounts, working with Systems and Data
• Run account moves and RoEs through the year, and turn one-off requests into a clear process with rules, templates and turnaround times
• Spot patterns in what breaks after a plan ships and feed them into the next plan's design
• Build tools and automations with Claude that remove manual work for the Strategy & Operations business partner community
You may be a good fit if you
• Deep alignment to Anthropic’s mission
• Direct experience with territory design
• Hands-on experience in sales planning, GTM strategy, revenue operations or a similar analytical role
• Advanced spreadsheet modeling, including building models that others can follow, audit and reuse
• Experience working with CRM data such as Salesforce, including accounts, ownership and hierarchies
• Ability to identify which assumptions matter most in a model and explain the downstream effects of changing them
• Experience running a process with many stakeholders to a fixed deadline
• Ability to earn the trust of field leaders and partner teams, and get work done through them without direct authority
• Track record of moving work forward through teams you don't manage
• Clear written and verbal communication with both field and leadership audiences
• Hands-on use of AI tools such as Claude to speed up analysis or remove manual work
Strong candidates may also
• Experience with planning at a company that was scaling its field team quickly
• Experience enriching CRM data or writing requirements for a systems team
• Experience with AI/ML companies and consumption business models

Location: Remote – Mid-Atlantic Region (must reside in VA, DC, MD, DE, PA, or NJ)
Sigma’s vision is to create an insight-driven world where people, organizations, and, ultimately, humanity are transformed for the better by data. At Sigma, we are building a cloud-native business intelligence platform that allows users to tap into their biggest databases hosted in the cloud and easily conduct ad hoc analysis to gain business insights in seconds. All without any SQL programming. We are growing the Solution Engineering team and are looking for a Solution Engineer who will help redefine the business intelligence landscape for our customers. You will join a talented team of Solution Engineers with a shared mission to truly make data access easy to drive business results.
The Sigma Solution Engineer believes in the power of analytics to transform organizations and uncover new data insights to increase business agility. The Sigma Solution Engineer will act as the trusted advisor to our prospects and customers working in tandem with Sales, Business Development, Product Management, Engineering, and Support. This individual is ultimately responsible for managing and delivering on all activities related to the technical presales cycle. This includes presentations, demonstrations, and hands on development of prototypes. You will align closely with our field Regional Sales Managers (Enterprise) focused on sales in new and existing accounts.
What You Will Be Doing
• Understand and uncover business challenges and issues faced by the customer and be able to run a targeted discovery sessions or workshop
• Engage with business users to define, create, and showcase solution prototypes
• Build and present customized demos for customers, trade shows, and webinars
• Confidently present and articulate the business value of the Sigma platform to all levels within an organization
• Deliver product, technical, and security related responses on RFPs/RFIs
• Participate in product, sales, and relevant technology certifications to acquire, maintain, and grow skill sets
• Work as a team player by contributing, learning, and sharing new knowledge
• Be conversant in integration and data migration approaches to facilitate enterprise-type sales cycles
• Manage multiple customer engagements concurrently
• Attain quarterly and annual objectives assigned by management
• Become a Sigma champion and product expert, prospects and customers will look to you for advice and expertise
Qualifications We Need
• Minimum 5 years of business intelligence experience
• Customer relationship skills
• Strong understanding of database concepts
• Cloud data warehouse experience - Snowflake, Redshift, BigQuery
• ETL experience - Fivetran, Matillion or traditional ETL
• Excellent organizational skills and ability to multitask in a fast-paced startup environment
• Experience implementing production business intelligence solutions or proof of concepts
• Bachelor’s degree in computer science or related field or equivalent technical & business experience
• 25% Travel
Qualifications We Want (also, skills you’ll learn!)
• Experience at a SaaS company or with cloud architectures
• Experience with data analytics business use cases
• Business consulting
• AI/Apps development experience
• Startup experience
About Sigma
Sigma is a modern analytics & business intelligence (BI) application built for the cloud. Trusted by data-first companies, Sigma provides live access to cloud data warehouses using an intuitive spreadsheet interface—empowering business experts to ask more of their data without writing a single line of code. With the full power of SQL, the cloud, and a familiar interface, business users have the freedom to analyze data in real time without limits. Sigma is self-service analytics as it was meant to be: a single source of truth that eliminates data extracts, simplifies analysis, and drives BI adoption at every level of business. Sigma is closing the gap between data teams and business experts. To learn more about Sigma, visit www.sigmacomputing.com or join the conversation on Twitter @SigmaComputing.
About us:
Sigma is the AI Apps and agentic analytics platform built on the cloud data warehouse. Business and technical teams use Sigma to explore live data, build intelligent applications, and automate critical workflows all without moving data or breaking governance. Sigma supports a spreadsheet interface, SQL, Python, and native AI in a single governed workspace, giving every team the speed to act and IT the control to scale. Sigma is trusted by more than 2,000 customers, including AMD, Duolingo, Colgate-Palmolive, and JPMorgan Chase.
Sigma announced its $80M in Series E financing in May 2026. The round was led by Princeville Capital, with new strategic investors Databricks Ventures, ServiceNow Ventures, and Workday Ventures participating alongside returning investors Altimeter Capital, Avenir Growth Capital, D1 Capital Partners, K5 Global, NewView Capital, Spark Capital, Sutter Hill Ventures, and XN. This milestone follows Sigma reaching $200M in annual recurring revenue in April 2026, with more than 100% year-over-year growth and 1.1 million new active users added in the latest fiscal year.
Come join us!
Benefits For Our Full-Time Employees:
• Equity
• Generous health benefits
• Flexible time off policy. Take the time off you need!
• Paid bonding time for all new parents
• Traditional and Roth 401k
• Commuter and FSA benefits
• Lunch Program
• Dog friendly office
Sigma is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a smart and strong team regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression, veteran, or any other protected status. We look forward to learning how your experience can enable all of us to grow.
Note: We have an in-office work environment in all our offices in SF, NYC, London and Sydney. All roles have a 25% travel expectation unless explicitly stated otherwise.
Our Privacy Practices
When you submit a job application on this site, Sigma processes your personal data for the purposes of evaluating your candidacy for employment at Sigma and as otherwise needed throughout the recruitment and hiring process. Please review Sigma’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more details. Please note that your personal data may be transferred to a country other than the one in which it was provided (including to the USA, the UK, and Canada, Australia).
Sigma’s use of AI
This hiring process utilizes artificial intelligence tools to assist in candidate screening and assessment. Our AI tools are designed to complement, not replace, human decision-making.

Fin , now part of Salesforce, is on a mission to help businesses provide perfect customer experiences.
Our AI Agent Fin is the highest-performing AI Customer Agent on the market today, enabling businesses to deliver impeccable, always-on customer support across the customer journey, from service, to sales, to ecommerce. Powered by our own AI models, Fin resolves complex customer issues end-to-end across every channel, with minimal set-up and integration. Fin can also be combined with our natively integrated Intercom help desk, giving modern support teams one single system.
Together with Salesforce, the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success, we're building the future of customer experience. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn't a buzzword, it's a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing, and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI.
Ready to level up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You're in the right place. Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.
What's the opportunity?
As Fin becomes mission-critical for our most strategic customers, we’re growing our team of Forward Deployed Engineers to help bridge the gap between customer needs and product innovation. This is a hybrid role based out of New York.
As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you’ll work hands-on with strategic customers, partnering closely with our R&D and Go-to-Market teams to design and deliver high-impact solutions. You’ll go beyond implementation - helping shape product direction, influence roadmap decisions and ensure Fin delivers real, measurable business outcomes in complex, real-world environments.
If you’re excited by ownership, creativity and solving ambiguous problems, and want to work at the frontier of applied AI while collaborating with Product, Engineering and Go-to-Market teams, this role offers a rare opportunity to combine technical excellence with real customer impact.
What will I be doing?
• Drive adoption of Fin by helping customers unlock the power of our AI capabilities to automate and scale their support operations.
• Embed deeply with strategic customers to understand their business challenges and technical requirements, and provide the insight needed to achieve outstanding results with Fin.
• Work hands-on with customers’ technical teams as a trusted technical expert, coding side-by-side to drive projects through to completion.
• Collaborate closely with Sales, Success and Product teams to ensure seamless customer experiences, successful project delivery and actionable product feedback.
• Contribute to the evolution of Forward Deployed Engineering by codifying best practices and sharing insights from customer engagements to help the team scale and grow.
What skills do I need?
• A strong engineering background and experience building software with real-world usage. Experience building a SaaS product is a plus, but not a requirement.
• Interest in AI and machine learning, and the ability to quickly build an understanding of novel problems, capabilities and architectures - including their trade-offs and limitations.
• Strong cross-functional collaboration skills, with the ability to navigate organisational boundaries and bring people together to achieve the best outcomes for our customers.
• Deep knowledge of at least one high-level programming language, such as JavaScript, Python or Ruby. It doesn’t need to be a language we use today - great people learn quickly and can introduce us to better ways of working.
• The ability to prototype and ship software quickly while maintaining a high bar for quality and a clear focus on business goals and outcomes.
• Proficiency using and writing REST APIs to integrate systems effectively.
• Strong communication skills. You can comfortably discuss the same topics with engineers and non-technical audiences, adapting the depth and detail as needed.
• Willingness to travel and work on-site with customers to build strong relationships and deeply understand their needs.
*Proof of eligibility to work in the United States is required.
The base salary range for candidates is $180,000 - $237,000. Actual base pay will depend on a variety of factors such as education, skills, experience, location, etc. The base pay range is subject to change and may be modified in the future. All regular employees may also be eligible for the corporate bonus program or a sales incentive (target included in OTE) as well as stock in the form of Restricted Stock Units (RSUs).
Unleash Your Potential
When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best, and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best. Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for AI, and the world.
In the United States, compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, job level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for incentive compensation, equity, and benefits. At Fin, we want to give people what they need to do the best work of their careers. Our benefits and programs are designed to support your health and wellbeing, your family, your time away from work, and your financial future. Offerings vary by location in line with local practices and requirements. Learn more about working at Fin and the benefits we offer at fin.ai/careers . Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance and the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring, Salesforce will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.
Policies
Fin has a hybrid working policy. We believe that working in person helps us stay connected, collaborate easier and create a great culture while still providing flexibility to work from home. We expect employees to be in the office at least three days per week.
We have a radically open and accepting culture at Fin. We avoid spending time on divisive subjects to foster a safe and cohesive work environment for everyone. As an organization, our policy is to not advocate on behalf of the company or our employees on any social or political topics out of our internal or external communications. We respect personal opinion and expression on these topics on personal social platforms on personal time, and do not challenge or confront anyone for their views on non-work related topics. Our goal is to focus on doing incredible work to achieve our goals and unite the company through our core values .
Salesforce is an equal opportunity employer and maintains a policy of non-discrimination with all employees and applicants for employment. What does that mean exactly? It means that at Salesforce, we believe in equality for all. And we believe we can lead the path to equality in part by creating a workplace that’s inclusive, and free from discrimination. Know your rights: workplace discrimination is illegal. Any employee or potential employee will be assessed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications – without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender expression or identity, transgender status, age, disability, veteran or marital status, political viewpoint, or other classifications protected by law. This policy applies to current and prospective employees, no matter where they are in their Salesforce employment journey. It also applies to recruiting, hiring, job assignment, compensation, promotion, benefits, training, assessment of job performance, discipline, termination, and everything in between. Recruiting, hiring, and promotion decisions at Salesforce are fair and based on merit. The same goes for compensation, benefits, promotions, transfers, reduction in workforce, recall, training, and education.

What's the opportunity?
Fin's GTM Data Science team builds the machine learning behind our Growth, Marketing and Sales teams. Our models decide which leads become MQLs, how they're routed, what they're worth, which play a rep runs next, how marketing spend is attributed, and which customers are ready to expand.
We already run many production models, including lead scoring, lead value, next best play, multi-touch attribution, marketing mix modeling and customer expansion. We're hiring a Data Scientist to own the day-to-day health of these production systems and to help turn prototypes into production models. This is not a reporting role. You'll ship changes that go live, and you'll see the effect on the pipeline.
If you want to work on applied ML in production, with real stakeholders and revenue on the line, this role is for you.
What will I be doing?
Own production models day to day
• Keep production GTM models healthy: inbound lead scoring and value, account and play recommendations, and marketing attribution and mix models
• Maintain the business logic around them: MQL routing tiers and exclusions, play eligibility rules and competitor overrides, and lead value tier bands
• Monitor performance, calibration, drift and data quality, and fix issues at their root cause: a broken enrichment feed, a tier mix that shifts overnight
• Write documentation and runbooks: how each model works, how to retrain it, and what to do when it breaks, so no model depends on one person
You keep the models the business relies on healthy and trusted.
Be the first point of contact for GTM stakeholders
• Answer questions from Growth, Marketing, Marketing Ops, SDR, Sales, CS and RevOps leaders, such as why a lead didn't MQL or why an account got a play
• Turn ad-hoc requests into scoped, prioritized work and well-tested changes
• Size a change's impact before it ships
• Build self-serve dashboards and monitoring so the same question doesn't come back
You make it easy for GTM teams to trust and act on our data products.
Ship new models into production
• Productionize prototypes built by senior data scientists into reliable, scheduled pipelines
• Integrate model outputs into the systems that act on them: Salesforce, ad platform conversion values, experimentation metrics and outbound play lists
• Set up the monitoring, alerting and tests each new model needs
• Measure lift after launch and report what changed
You'll learn how a model goes from notebook to production, and own that path.
What impact might I have
Within 6-12 months, you might:
• Be the named owner of one or more production models, end to end
• Cut the time from a stakeholder question to a shipped fix from days to hours
• Catch data-quality breaks before they cost us MQLs or pipeline
• Ship at least one prototype into production and measure its lift
Success is measured in model health, stakeholder trust and business outcomes.

Experience
• 1-3 years in data science, analytics engineering, ML engineering or a related quantitative role (internships and graduate research count)
• Some experience with a model or data pipeline that ran in production, or a strong wish to learn
• Exposure to GTM data (Growth, Marketing, Sales) in a B2B SaaS setting is a plus
Technical skills
• Strong SQL and Python for data analysis and modeling (pandas, scikit-learn or similar)
• Solid foundations in statistics: distributions, hypothesis testing, model evaluation
• Comfort with version control (GitHub) and code review
• Familiarity with dbt, Snowflake, Airflow or Salesforce is a plus
Mindset
You are:
• An owner: you follow an issue to its root cause and close the loop with the person who raised it
• Careful: you check your numbers, test changes before they ship, and say clearly what you're unsure of
• Curious: you dig into the "why" when a metric moves

• Eager to grow: you learn from senior data scientists and take on more scope quickly

The team + the role
Pendo’s Data & AI Platform team turns raw data into the insights the business runs on. Our analytics engineers have moved beyond one-off analyses: they build and operate AI-powered data products that teams across the company rely on every day, all built on a shared dbt semantic layer that feeds BI dashboards, internal applications, and operationalized production AI agents. In this role, you will own the architecture behind one of those products, from the data model and semantic layer through service boundaries, and make reliability and security decisions independently. You will define the technical approach to team goals and help the whole team get more out of AI-assisted engineering.
What you own
• Data product architecture: Own the end-to-end architecture of an analytics or AI product, including data modeling, semantic-layer design, and service boundaries. Solve the team’s hardest problems where reliability, design, and security intersect.
• Shared semantic layer: Architect the dbt semantic layer that powers BI dashboards, internal applications, and AI agents. Lead cross-team metric consolidation so every metric has a single, trusted definition.
Data pipelines and ingestion: Design and maintain reliable ELT/ETL pipelines that bring data from SaaS applications, production databases, and event streams into the warehouse, using batch, incremental, and change data capture (CDC) patterns. Own orchestration, scheduling, and data contracts with upstream source owners. Warehouse modeling and performance: Build layered, well-tested data models (staging, intermediate, and mart layers using dimensional or medallion patterns) in a cloud data warehouse or lakehouse. Tune SQL, incremental models, partitioning, and clustering for cost, performance, and point-in-time correctness.
• Security and reliability: Serve as a security reviewer for what the team ships: own the authentication model, review pull requests and service architecture for exposure, and design to minimize attack surface. Help set standards for the scalability, stability, and continuous improvement of the semantic layer and the products built on it.
• Mentorship and team elevation: Mentor teammates, as well as engineers from outside the data organization who are contributing to shared infrastructure for the first time. Raise the bar for the team’s AI-assisted engineering practices and play an active role in recruiting.
• Cross-functional leadership: Where business strategy is set but the technical path is not, define the approach before being asked. Break complex work into clear milestones, help stakeholders understand how it affects them, and lead cross-functional initiatives through to delivery.
Success will be measured by
• First 30 days: You have completed a diagnostic of the product and semantic layer you will own, covering strengths, gaps, security exposure, and the highest-leverage next improvement. You have a clear point of view on technical direction.
• First quarter (90 days): You own the end-to-end architecture of at least one production analytics or AI product. You have shipped a meaningful improvement to it or to the underlying semantic layer, and your design decisions are holding up in production.
• Reliable insight delivery: The product you own is accurate and available. When it breaks or produces incorrect results, you treat it as an incident, diagnose the root cause through logs and tracing, and fix it.
• Team elevation: Teammates and contributors ship safer, more reliable work because of your reviews, mentorship, and standards, and the team’s AI-assisted engineering practices have improved as a result.
• Architecture durability: Your data modeling and semantic-layer decisions hold up as new use cases and consumers come online. Metrics are consolidated rather than duplicated, and you catch problems before they escalate.
How we work
Builder mindset
Pendo’s Data & AI team operates on a builder-first model. A builder moves without being told what to do next. They see ambiguity and start solving. It is not about technical skill. It is a posture. These are the four competencies we hire for, develop against, and evaluate on:
• Bias to Act (Judgment). When a modeling or architecture tradeoff has no clear right answer, you make the call, document your reasoning, and own the outcome. You make security and reliability decisions without waiting for escalation, and you prioritize by business impact, not request order.
• Maniacal Focus (Velocity). Improvements ship without stalling in design review. You break complex projects into clear milestones and safely mergeable increments, balancing long-term semantic-layer architecture with near-term delivery.
• Hone Your Craft (AI Fluency). AI-assisted engineering is a core part of how you model, test, and review code, and you help raise the team’s standard, not just your own. You bring technical depth to AI fluency, engaging on architecture and capability tradeoffs rather than surface-level familiarity. Tools will change; what matters is being comfortable learning while the ground moves.
• Team is Pendo (Impact & Ownership). Teams across Pendo depend on your product and the semantic layer beneath it every day. When you see a pattern being misused, you fix the pattern, not just the instance. You mentor on the why, not just the how, including engineers outside the data organization. Your impact extends beyond your own code to the whole team.
Who you are
Must-haves

We’re looking for a As the Manager of Sales Compensation Systems and Analytics, you’ll operate at the center of go-to-market execution —- owning the systems, data, and analytics that power how Fivetran + dbt labs pays its sellers and measures performance against quota. You’ll build and scale the compensation infrastructure, deliver accurate and timely commissions, and provide insights that inform plan design and executive decisions. You’ll partner closely with Sales Leadership, Revenue Operations, Sales Strategy, Revenue Accounting, Payroll, Legal, and Analytics.
This role reports to the Sr. Director, Global Sales Compensation and blends sales compensation administration, systems ownership, data analytics, and operational execution. You’ll drive the automation and accuracy of our commission processes, help scale our compensation platform for a hybrid pricing motion that includes both subscription contracts and usage-based (consumption) revenue, and support high-visibility initiatives across the function.
This is a high-impact role ideal for someone who is passionate about leveraging systems, data, and analytics to motivate sales performance and drive operational excellence in a high-growth, cross-functional environment.

What You’ll Do
• Compensation Systems Ownership: Own the configuration, administration, and roadmap of our sales compensation platform (e.g., Xactly, CaptivateIQ, Varicent, or similar), including plan builds, crediting rules, quota and territory loads, and integrations with Salesforce, the data warehouse, and HRIS/Payroll. Partner with Systems and IT on releases, testing, and enhancements.
• Commission Operations: Oversee the end-to-end monthly and quarterly commission calculation, validation, and payout cycle, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and compliance with plan documents, including crediting for subscription and consumption-based bookings, overages, and renewals
• Plan Design Support: Partner with Sales Strategy, Finance, and GTM leadership to model, build, and launch annual and in-year compensation plans, quota structures, and SPIFs; quantify cost of sales and the financial impact of plan changes.
• Analytics & Insights: Deliver analysis on plan effectiveness, attainment distribution, pay-for-performance alignment, quota capacity, and comp cost as a percent of ARR/bookings to inform decisions by the CRO, CFO, and Sales Leadership.
• Accruals & Forecasting: Partner closely with Revenue Accounting and FP&A on commission accruals, ASC 340-40 capitalization, variance analysis, and forecast-to-actual tracking of variable compensation expense.
• Governance & Controls: Own SOX-compliant controls, audit readiness, plan documentation, and dispute resolution processes; ensure data integrity and reconciliation between source systems, the comp platform, and payroll.
• Automation & Reporting Infrastructure: Use AI tools, SQL (BigQuery), or Python to automate data pulls, build repeatable and auditable processes, and improve the accuracy, speed, and transparency of commission calculations; partner with Analytics, AI Transformation, and Systems on data quality and self-serve reporting.
• Seller Experience & Reporting: Create automated, executive-ready dashboards and statements (e.g., Looker, Tableau) that give sellers and managers clear, real-time visibility into attainment, earnings, and pipeline-to-pay, and that distill trends into actionable recommendations for GTM leadership.
• Team Leadership: Provide technical guidance, review work, and help raise the process and analytical standards of the Sales Compensation team
Skills We’re Looking For
• 5-7 years of experience in sales compensation, sales operations, revenue operations, or FP&A, with hands-on administration of a compensation platform
• Expert-level analytical modeling: builds compensation models from scratch, including cost-of-program scenarios, pay-positioning analysis, attrition and retention-risk modeling, and sensitivity and tradeoff analysis
• Built with AI: has personally used AI tools (LLMs, assistants, or automation and agent platforms) to build compensation tools, models, or workflows others rely on, and can explain how they work and how outputs were checked for accuracy
• Technical aptitude: working proficiency in SQL, Python, or similar scripting; experience with Salesforce, BI tools (e.g., Looker), and data warehouses (e.g., BigQuery, Snowflake) a plus
• Statistical judgment: knows when market data is credible or a sample is too small, and presents ranges without false precision
• Compensation expertise: job architecture, compensation frameworks, market pricing, pay cycles, global compensation practices, and pay-for-performance design, with knowledge of competitor compensation at high-growth tech companies
• Reasons from first principles: balances best practice with what the business needs and can rebuild a framework when the standard approach does not fit
• Trusted advisor to senior leaders on sensitive, high-stakes compensation decisions (offers, promotions, retention, org changes), influencing outcomes through data and judgment rather than authority
• Operational excellence: connects systems, stakeholders, and programs to deliver compensation end to end, accurately and on time
• Clear communicator: turns complex analysis into a crisp recommendation an executive can act on in one conversation
• Experience with usage-based or consumption pricing models and the associated compensation design challenges strongly preferred
Bonus Skills​
• Experience with Tableau or other BI tools, or building dashboards for leaders
• Experience supporting GTM or sales organizations at a high-growth tech company
• Experience scaling compensation programs through hypergrowth, IPO, or major organizational change
• Background in a quantitative field (e.g., finance, statistics, engineering), or equivalent experience

• Strong written and verbal communication, with the confidence to present to sellers and to Pricing Strategy, Product, and Sales leaders

Manager, Commercial Operations

We are looking for a Manager of Commercial Operations to build and run the transactional engine of the commercial function inside Revenue Operations. ClickHouse runs on a usage-based pricing model, and every deal – direct, marketplace, or partner – has to land correctly in the system: quoted against the right rules, ordered against the right contract structure, and booked cleanly enough that Accounting can bill and recognize it without rework. As we scale the cloud business and widen the product line, that path has to carry more volume, more products, and more deal structures without adding people to the middle of it. This role designs the systems, automation, and controls that make that possible.

Reporting to the Senior Director, Commercial Strategy & Operations, you will own the quote-to-order path and order management, along with the build behind it: the CPQ and quoting system requirements, the automation, the validation and controls, and marketplace transaction operations across AWS, GCP, and Azure. The goal is a commercial path where the standard deal is self-service for the field, quality is enforced by the system rather than by who touched the deal, and human review is reserved for the cases that genuinely need judgment. You will be measured by how fast and how cleanly a deal moves, how little intervention it requires, and how good the experience is for the rep. You will partner daily with Sales, Accounting, Finance, Legal, and Revenue Engineering.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

 - Own order management and automate it. Run the intake, review, and processing of quotes, order forms, and bookings to defined SLAs through quarter-end peaks, and continuously engineer the manual steps out of that path.

 - Design the quote-to-order flow. Instrument the process, find where it slows or breaks, and redesign it. You own the architecture of the flow, the exception routing, and the automation that makes the standard case hands-off.

 - Own the quoting and order management system build. Write the requirements, design the quoting, validation, and approval logic, drive the roadmap with Revenue Engineering, run UAT, and validate every change in production before the field sees it.

 - Own the handoff into billing and revenue. Partner with Accounting so that what leaves your process arrives structured, complete, and reconcilable – and build the controls upstream that keep downstream rework from happening at all.

 - Build quality in as controls. Validation rules, guided quoting, required-field logic, and automated reconciliation that make an incorrect order hard to submit in the first place.

 - Own the field experience of transacting. Treat the rep as the customer: fewer steps, fewer handoffs, shorter quote cycle time, and a standard path that is obvious and self-service. Measure whether it is getting easier.

 - Build and run marketplace transaction operations across AWS, GCP, and Azure. Private offers, CSP transactions, co-sell mechanics, and the tooling and automated reconciliation that keep marketplace bookings tied out across the marketplace, Salesforce, and billing.

 - Operationalize commercial review. Encode approval rules and guardrails in the system so routine deals route themselves, and escalate the structures that break the system rather than quietly processing them.

 - Build the transaction path for new products and acquisitions. Stand up order management, quoting, and the marketplace path for new offerings and newly acquired products, test the flow through to booking before go-live, and be ready to transact on day one.

 - Own the integrity of the commercial record. Products, SKUs, pricing, contract terms, and booking attributes in Salesforce, with the controls and monitoring that keep them clean – the forecast and revenue reporting downstream depend on it.

 - Instrument and report on the system you own. Cycle time, touch count, SLA attainment, exception and discount volumes, error and rework rates. Use the data to decide what gets built next.

WHAT YOU BRING ALONG

 - 6+ years in commercial operations, deal desk, order management, sales operations, or revenue operations, including time owning a high-volume transactional process.

 - A track record of building, not just running. You have replaced a manual process with a designed one and can point to the automation, the controls, and the measured result.

 - Hands-on depth in Salesforce and Salesforce CPQ. You write requirements, design quoting and approval logic, configure and test it yourself, and can tell a configuration problem from a process problem.

 - Technical range beyond the admin console: flows and validation logic, API-based and marketplace integrations, and scripting or SQL to reconcile and investigate data at volume. You can partner with Revenue Engineering as a peer on design.

 - Experience with usage-based or consumption-based contracts: metering, commits, overages, contract structure, and the downstream billing and revenue recognition implications.

 - Experience operating across a shared quote-to-cash process. You know where order management ends and Accounting begins, and you design the handoff so neither side is cleaning up after the other.

 - Marketplace operations experience with AWS, GCP, or Azure – private offers, CSP transactions, and reconciliation – strongly preferred.

 - Process-engineering instincts. You instrument before you optimize, design for the standard case and route the exception, and measure by throughput and error rate rather than activity.

 - A bias toward field experience. You have made a transactional process materially faster or simpler for a sales team and can describe how you knew it worked.

 - Comfort partnering with Accounting, Finance, and Legal on order form and contract mechanics.

 - Sound judgment under deal pressure. You can hold the line on a structure that breaks the system, and advocate for the field when the exception is justified.

 - Clear written and verbal communication. You can explain a commercial rule to a rep in one paragraph and brief leadership on what's at risk at quarter-end.

 - Experience managing or mentoring analysts a plus; this role is expected to grow a team as volume scales.

 - Bachelor's degree, quantitative or technical field preferred.

Check out our blog posts https://clickhouse.com/blog or follow us on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/clickhouseinc/life/0c1ee7f4-2129-488d-b413-e7f6270659fd/?viewAsMember=true to find out more about what’s happening at ClickHouse.

As our retailer relationships scale and the complexity of our business deepens, we need someone who can support the data and analytics layer for the entire Commercial organization. We're hiring a Business Intelligence Manager II to build the data and AI foundation the Commercial org runs on: the models, semantic layer, dashboards, and AI tools that let analysts go deeper and let partner managers get trusted answers. This individual contributor role is the first hire in a new Data & AI function for Commercial Partnerships, with room to grow as it scales. The role will partner closely with our Commercial Insights and Partnerships teams, and the work will shape how Instacart grows its most important partnerships.
WHAT YOU'LL COOK UP IN YOUR FIRST YEAR
• Analysts move faster because of your foundation. Core 1P and 3P data is modeled, tested, and documented. You work with Data Engineering to maintain and extend our retail data layer, so analysts spend their time on insight, not on reconciling numbers.
• Third-party data is a trusted asset. You manage our 3P data partnerships and maintain source-of-truth documentation and examples, so technical teams across the company use it consistently.
• Non-technical stakeholders self-serve. Partner Managers and Strategy & Planning stakeholders get accurate answers through dashboards and AI tools built on the semantic layer, with the guardrails and evals that make them trustworthy. You know your users, built what they actually use, and can show adoption.
• Repeat requests become products. You've turned recurring asks into self-serve tools, and you can show the hours saved or the requests that stopped coming.
• Cross-functional teams are better equipped to answer "why" and "what's next." You've built tools and frameworks that help stakeholders move from raw data to clear direction.
• You're the go-to expert on commercial data. Teams rely on you for where data comes from, what it means, and its caveats, including first- and third-party sources.
THE SECRET INGREDIENTS WE'RE LOOKING FOR
You sit between data and the business. You're as comfortable modeling data as you are sitting with an account manager to understand what they actually need, and you measure success by how many people can answer their own questions because of what you built.
Must-have pantry staples (Minimum Qualifications)
• 5+ years of experience in business intelligence, data analytics, or analytics engineering, building data products (models, dashboards, and self-serve tools) for business stakeholders.
• Strong SQL and solid data modeling fundamentals: choosing the right grain, designing fact and dimension tables, and handling data that changes over time.
• Hands-on experience with a modern data stack (e.g. dbt, Snowflake, Airflow).
• Experience with modern BI platforms and a track record of building reliable, effective tools and dashboards.
• Hands-on use of LLMs or AI tools in data workflows.
• Strong communication and stakeholder management. You turn ambiguous business questions into data requirements, explain data caveats to non-technical audiences, and reshape requests when needed.
• A self-starter orientation — you don't wait to be handed a problem; you identify it, frame it, and drive toward an answer.
Optional garnishes (Preferred Qualifications)
• Experience in retail, e-commerce, or grocery — familiarity with the dynamics of online marketplaces is a meaningful accelerant.
• Experience partnering with sales, account management, or partnerships teams.
• Experience managing data from external vendors or third-party providers.
• Experience with semantic data layers or metric frameworks.
• Experience building AI data agents or LLM apps, including evaluation and guardrails.

Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
The Community You Will Join:
Our Product Managers imagine the ideal experience for our community and work backwards, creating innovative products that delight our guests and hosts. They deeply understand the needs of our users and translate these into a strategy that combines strong product thinking and deep research. They partner with talented cross-functional team members across engineering, design, operations, data science, and more, leading teams to execute a shared vision. They are incredibly detail-oriented and hands on.
The Guest product team owns and builds the end-to-end journey guests take to travel with us, from the first idea through the trip itself. Trip planning is where that journey becomes intelligent: a team of engineers, applied researchers, designers, and data scientists building an AI planning agent that can understand what guests are looking for, and reason across homes, experiences, services and more to assemble a real trip. We're building toward a future where Airbnb feels like a knowledgeable travel companion that plans alongside you.
The Difference You Will Make:
As Product Manager for AI trip planning, you will own the strategy and execution for this agent — one of Airbnb's most ambitious bets on an AI-native product. You'll define what it means for an agent to plan a trip well: how it asks the right questions, reasons about tradeoffs guests care about, and turns intent into a bookable trip spanning homes, experiences, and services. You’ll take the product from a demo to a system millions of guests rely on, and the work will be measured in bookings across categories and guest satisfaction at global scale. You’ll communicate these new AI features to the world by distilling the complex ideas into simple, delightful, and well-received products.
A Typical Day:
• Define and drive the roadmap for a multi-turn agent that can plan trips with guests along their travel journey
• Set the quality bar for agent behavior: what a good plan looks like, where the agent should defer to the guest, and how it recovers when it's wrong
• Own the cross-category planning problem and sequence work with Homes, Experiences, Services, and Hotels so the agent can plan across the full inventory
• Work with ML engineers and applied researchers on model strategy, evaluation frameworks, and experiment design
• Make prioritization calls when guest trust, planning quality, latency, cost, marketplace health, and revenue pull against each other
• Keep cross-functional partners such as Search & Discovery, Relevance & Personalization, Trips, Trust & Safety, Customer Support, Legal, and Privacy aligned on shared goals and sequencing
• Design A/B experiments and offline evals, including proxy metrics for planning quality and measurement of long-term effects
• Turn complex technical tradeoffs into clear decisions for engineering teams and concise narratives for leadership
• Stay close to guests: synthesize user research, planning-session data, and competitive signals to sharpen your intuition and refine strategy
• Partner with marketing and communications to bring each release to market, and craft the product narrative that explains it to leadership internally and to guests externally
Your Expertise:
• 10+ years of consumer product management experience, including meaningful time on AI/ML, search, recommendations, or conversational products at scale
• A track record of owning strategy, setting direction for technically complex systems, and making tough prioritization decisions
• Experience shipping LLM-based products in production, including the evaluation, latency, cost, and guardrail work that stands between a good demo and a launch
• Fluent in experimentation: you can evaluate A/B test results and offline eval honestly, and reason about proxy metrics versus long-term outcomes
• Strong judgment of consumer product quality; you can tell the difference between an agent that sounds impressive and one that’s useful
• Experience working on two-sided marketplaces or platforms where you balanced supply-side and demand-side tradeoffs
• Ability to earn the respect of Staff and Principal-level engineers and researchers
• Clear, structured communicator who can distill complex technical tradeoffs for executives and translate strategic intent into actionable guidance for engineers
• Experience with agentic systems: tool use, planning and orchestration, retrieval, or multi-turn state management (preferred)

The Trade Desk is a global technology company and the world’s leading independent platform for digital advertising, with over 3,000 employees across more than 30 offices. Our technology helps advertisers reach the right audiences across the open internet — from streaming TV and podcasts to mobile apps, news, and more.
Advertising powers the content people love. By making it more transparent, effective, and responsible, we help support trusted journalism, quality entertainment, and creators worldwide. The world’s brands and agencies rely on us to reach their customers and grow their businesses responsibly.
The scale of our platform brings unique technical challenges — from processing massive datasets in real time to building systems that operate reliably on a global scale. When you work here, your impact is worldwide. We welcome diverse perspectives, encourage curiosity, and build teams that learn from one another. If you’re driven to solve meaningful challenges, we’d love to meet you.
What we do:
You’ll join a software engineering team that builds internal AI solutions supporting teams across The Trade Desk. We use large language models (LLMs), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agentic systems, custom MCP servers, and enterprise platforms like Anthropic Claude to improve productivity, streamline workflows, and reduce operational friction.
Our team also plays a key role in AI enablement across the company—supporting teams as they adopt Copilot, Claude and similar tools, designing and deploying custom AI agents, and guiding partners through their AI journey from idea to impact.
As a Senior AI Enablement Engineer on this team, you’ll be an end-to-end owner—collaborating closely with stakeholders, identifying opportunities, and delivering tools that make a real impact. We’re a nimble, fast-paced, and highly collaborative group that thrives on transforming the way teams operate and driving greater value across The Trade Desk.
What you'll do:
Some of the work that you will be doing to help us deliver on our mission is:
• Partner with Business teams across The Trade Desk to understand Business processes, identify opportunities, scope and prioritize use cases, and define success metrics before building.
• Design and build agents and agentic workflows, including background and conversational agents, that orchestrate tools, data, and business processes end to end to solve real-world problems and deliver measurable business value within enterprise guardrails.
• Design and build custom MCP servers that securely expose enterprise data, APIs, and internal systems to AI agents, with well-designed tool schemas, proper authentication, least-privilege permission scoping, and observability.
• Design and deploy intelligent agentic systems that integrate large language models (LLMs) with enterprise data, tools, and workflows using modern agent SDKs and orchestration frameworks.
• Rapidly prototype, validate with real users, then harden the winners into supported solutions or hand them off to the owning team.
• Drive adoption through training, office hours, playbooks, reusable templates, and reference implementations that other teams can self-serve from.
• Drive quality and performance through automated testing, evaluation suites, monitoring, and data-driven evaluation of success criteria, user adoption, cost, and operational efficiency.
• Mentor teammates and contribute to a culture of innovation, technical excellence, and continuous learning.
Who you are:
• You have a Bachelor's/Master's level degree in computer science or relevant engineering-related field or equivalent experience.
• You have 6-8+ years of experience in software engineering, forward deployed engineering, solutions engineering, or technical consulting, including 1-2+ years building LLM-powered solutions that reached real users in production.
• You are proficient in Python and/or TypeScript and comfortable with additional languages such as C# or SQL.
• You're excited about AI, including helping teams adopt Anthropic Claude, building agents, workflows and MCP servers, and guiding others through their AI journey.
• You have hands-on experience with LLM APIs, tool use, and prompt engineering, and you've built MCP servers or equivalent function-calling integrations, or can show you'd ramp up quickly.
• You have experience with enterprise identity and access, including OAuth, SSO/Entra ID, and scoping permissions so an agent can only do what the user is allowed to do.
• You have experience productionizing applications and implementing CI/CD pipelines to ensure reliable, scalable deployments.
• You are skilled in data ingestion and transformation using APIs, ETL pipelines, and connectors, and familiar with vector databases and retrieval strategies.
• You treat evaluation and safety as core engineering work, including evals, tracing, prompt-injection defenses, and cost and latency management.
• You communicate clearly across technical and non-technical audiences, can run discovery sessions and demos with business partners, and thrive in a collaborative, cross-functional environment.
• You are a fast learner who adapts quickly to new technologies and solves complex problems with creativity and pragmatism.

The Trade Desk is a global technology company and the world’s leading independent platform for digital advertising, with over 3,000 employees across more than 30 offices. Our technology helps advertisers reach the right audiences across the open internet — from streaming TV and podcasts to mobile apps, news, and more.
Advertising powers the content people love. By making it more transparent, effective, and responsible, we help support trusted journalism, quality entertainment, and creators worldwide. The world’s brands and agencies rely on us to reach their customers and grow their businesses responsibly.
The scale of our platform brings unique technical challenges — from processing massive datasets in real time to building systems that operate reliably on a global scale. When you work here, your impact is worldwide. We welcome diverse perspectives, encourage curiosity, and build teams that learn from one another. If you’re driven to solve meaningful challenges, we’d love to meet you.
What we do:
You’ll join a software engineering team that builds internal AI solutions supporting teams across The Trade Desk. We use large language models (LLMs), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agentic systems, custom MCP servers, and enterprise platforms like Anthropic Claude to improve productivity, streamline workflows, and reduce operational friction.
Our team also plays a key role in AI enablement across the company—supporting teams as they adopt Copilot, Claude and similar tools, designing and deploying custom AI agents, and guiding partners through their AI journey from idea to impact.
As a Senior Forward Deployed Engineer on this team, you’ll be an end-to-end owner—collaborating closely with stakeholders, identifying opportunities, and delivering tools that make a real impact. We’re a nimble, fast-paced, and highly collaborative group that thrives on transforming the way teams operate and driving greater value across The Trade Desk.
What you'll do:
Some of the work that you will be doing to help us deliver on our mission is:
• Partner with Business teams across The Trade Desk to understand Business processes, identify opportunities, scope and prioritize use cases, and define success metrics before building.
• Design and build agents and agentic workflows, including background and conversational agents, that orchestrate tools, data, and business processes end to end to solve real-world problems and deliver measurable business value within enterprise guardrails.
• Design and build custom MCP servers that securely expose enterprise data, APIs, and internal systems to AI agents, with well-designed tool schemas, proper authentication, least-privilege permission scoping, and observability.
• Design and deploy intelligent agentic systems that integrate large language models (LLMs) with enterprise data, tools, and workflows using modern agent SDKs and orchestration frameworks.
• Rapidly prototype, validate with real users, then harden the winners into supported solutions or hand them off to the owning team.
• Drive adoption through training, office hours, playbooks, reusable templates, and reference implementations that other teams can self-serve from.
• Drive quality and performance through automated testing, evaluation suites, monitoring, and data-driven evaluation of success criteria, user adoption, cost, and operational efficiency.
• Mentor teammates and contribute to a culture of innovation, technical excellence, and continuous learning.
Who you are:
• You have a Bachelor's/Master's level degree in computer science or relevant engineering-related field or equivalent experience.
• You have 6-8+ years of experience in software engineering, forward deployed engineering, solutions engineering, or technical consulting, including 1-2+ years building LLM-powered solutions that reached real users in production.
• You are proficient in Python and/or TypeScript and comfortable with additional languages such as C# or SQL.
• You're excited about AI, including helping teams adopt Anthropic Claude, building agents, workflows and MCP servers, and guiding others through their AI journey.
• You have hands-on experience with LLM APIs, tool use, and prompt engineering, and you've built MCP servers or equivalent function-calling integrations, or can show you'd ramp up quickly.
• You have experience with enterprise identity and access, including OAuth, SSO/Entra ID, and scoping permissions so an agent can only do what the user is allowed to do.
• You have experience productionizing applications and implementing CI/CD pipelines to ensure reliable, scalable deployments.
• You are skilled in data ingestion and transformation using APIs, ETL pipelines, and connectors, and familiar with vector databases and retrieval strategies.
• You treat evaluation and safety as core engineering work, including evals, tracing, prompt-injection defenses, and cost and latency management.
• You communicate clearly across technical and non-technical audiences, can run discovery sessions and demos with business partners, and thrive in a collaborative, cross-functional environment.
• You are a fast learner who adapts quickly to new technologies and solves complex problems with creativity and pragmatism.

About the Team
The Dasher & Logistics team ensures every delivery is completed with speed, accuracy, and a positive experience for consumers, merchants, and Dashers. We own the health of DoorDash’s delivery network, including supply and demand, cost and quality, Dasher pay and incentives, Dasher acquisition and retention, assignment and batching, and real-time operations.
Within Strategy & Operations, Dasher & Logistics is made up of teams that each own part of this system, such as Network Strategy, US Markets, Regulated Markets, Canada, Supply, Pay & Efficiency, and Live Ops. We partner closely with Product, Engineering, Analytics, Finance, Marketing, and Operations to run and improve one of the largest last-mile logistics networks in the world.
About the Role
We’re hiring a Senior Manager, Strategy & Operations to own a meaningful part of the Dasher & Logistics network end-to-end. Depending on the team, that could be how we invest in Dasher supply, the health of every US market, our most complex regulated markets, or the delivery network for an entire country. You will be accountable for the cost-to-quality tradeoff in your area: faster, more reliable deliveries at the same cost, or the same quality at a lower cost.
You will find where the network underperforms, design and test the fix, and work with Product and Engineering to build it into how the network runs. You will make tradeoff decisions across Dasher earnings, consumer experience, merchant reliability, and unit economics, and bring clear recommendations to senior leadership. You will also build and develop a team that can take on more over time.
Success in this role means consistently delivering a faster, more reliable delivery experience while improving cost efficiency, and making changes that last because they are built into our products and operating rhythm.
You will report into a Director or Senior Director on our Dasher & Logistics team within Strategy & Operations. We expect this role to be hybrid, with some time in-office and some time remote.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
• Own business outcomes for your area, including delivery speed, quality, cost per delivery, and supply-demand balance, as the single DRI for those metrics in weekly business reviews and half-year planning
• Get to the lowest level of detail to diagnose where the network underperforms, by market, submarket, or zone, and explain why the metrics moved
• Manage key logistics levers, such as Dasher pay and incentives, supply programs, assignment and batching, delivery distance, and scheduling
• Design and run experiments that lead to clear decisions, then scale what works across markets
• Partner with Product, Engineering, and Analytics to turn manual wins into durable product and system changes
• Make thoughtful tradeoff decisions between cost, growth, and customer experience to protect long-term marketplace health
• Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing team, and grow the next set of leaders at DoorDash
• Help keep the network running smoothly during incidents, severe weather, and holidays alongside our Live Ops partners
We’re excited about you because…
• You have 8+ years of experience in strategy & operations, management consulting, finance, marketplace or logistics operations, or another analytically demanding field
• You have owned complex business areas with accountability for cost, quality, and financial results
• You are highly analytical and comfortable in the raw data, including writing SQL and building models in spreadsheets
• You use AI as a default part of how you work, building analyses, models, and prototype tools yourself to move faster
• You lead cross-functionally without formal authority and get teams that don’t report to you to adopt a shared plan
• You turn complex analysis into clear recommendations for executives, and you change course quickly when the results say you should
• You have managed and developed high-performing teams
• Bonus: experience with two- or three-sided marketplaces, gig or contractor-based labor models, last-mile delivery, or operating across markets with different regulatory dynamics

Every day, tens of millions of people come to Roblox to explore, create, play, learn, and connect with friends in 3D immersive digital experiences– all created by our global community of developers and creators.
At Roblox, we’re building the tools and platform that empower our community to bring any experience that they can imagine to life. Our vision is to reimagine the way people come together, from anywhere in the world, and on any device. We’re on a mission to connect a billion people with optimism and civility, and looking for amazing talent to help us get there.
A career at Roblox means you’ll be working to shape the future of human interaction, solving unique technical challenges at scale, and helping to create safer, more civil shared experiences for everyone.
WHY DATA SCIENCE & ANALYTICS?
The Data Science & Analytics organization's mission is to increase our speed, frequency and accuracy of making decisions at scale by instilling a data-influenced approach to building products. We cover a wide area of the data spectrum including analytical data engineering, product analytics, experimentation, causal inference, statistical modeling and machine learning. Aligned and partnering with product verticals, we use this tool belt to discover new opportunities and unmet use cases, influence and shape the product roadmap and prioritization, build data products and measure impact on our community of players and developers.
WHY TRUST & SAFETY?
With our large and growing number of active users on Roblox, we are an ever more attractive target for malicious actors to both compromise user accounts and proliferate fake accounts for the purposes of spam and phishing. Using a combination of machine learning and engineering, you'll develop new techniques and signals to help automatically identify repeated bad actors across a set of accounts as quickly as possible and identify common patterns to proactively prevent future abuse.
You Are :
• Highly self-driven. You are perpetually curious and consistently strive to improve your skills by learning the latest modeling techniques and data tools. You thrive with freedom and autonomy and are excited by exploring new problem spaces.
• A strong communicator. You understand that analysis must be presented in meaningful ways and engage in spirited discussions about the findings. You have the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences and discuss appropriate tradeoffs.
• Motivated by impact. You find great satisfaction in being able to point to direct contributions you've made to an organization. You recognize the inherent tradeoffs between further research/experimentation and productionization apply the appropriate methodology to maximize impact.
• Experienced in developing models and interest in taking work from research to production. You are capable of using machine learning and statistical techniques to model a variety of different types of data from time-series and sequential data to unstructured data like text and images.
You Will :
• Reporting to the Senior Director, you will accelerate product development through your understanding of the underlying data and your ability to partner with product and technical leaders to provide insights that lead to the safest experiences for Roblox's sizable user base.
• Investigate new ways to discover automated behavior on the Roblox platform.
• Develop modeling solutions to identify new attacks and signals of malicious user behavior.
• Collaborate with engineering teams to push detection systems toward real-time identification.
Basic Qualifications :
• Possess or pursuing a PhD in Computer Science, Applied Math, Physics, Engineering, Statistics, Economics or other technical field
• Experience in statistical modeling and machine learning
• Experience with deep learning/modern ML techniques
Preferred Qualifications :
• Problem Solving: Ability to frame ambiguous problems, designing analytical approaches, and solving open-ended data science problems that could drive business impact.
• Training or fine-tuning machine learning models

About Faire
Faire is a technology wholesale platform built on the belief that the future is local. Independent retailers around the globe collectively represent a multi-hundred-billion-dollar wholesale market that has historically been fragmented and offline. At Faire, we're using the power of tech, data, and machine learning to connect this thriving community of entrepreneurs across the globe. Picture your favorite boutique in town — we help them discover the best products from around the world to sell in their stores. With the right tools and insights, we believe that we can level the playing field so businesses can grow and local communities can thrive.
We’re looking for smart, resourceful and passionate people to join us as we power the shop local movement. If you believe in community, come join ours.
About this role
Faire leverages the power of machine learning and data insights to revolutionize the wholesale industry, enabling local retailers to compete against giants like Amazon and big box stores. Our highly skilled team of Applied AI/ML Scientists specialize in developing algorithmic solutions for notification and recommender systems, advertising attribution, and LTV predictions. We are dedicated to building machine learning models that help our customers thrive.
As a Senior Applied AI/ML Scientist on the Retailer Growth team, you will own the modeling and measurement for problems that shape the retailer experience after signup: helping new retailers get started on Faire, and helping retailers build relationships with more brands over time. Because our users are businesses, there is a wealth of information about them that ML models can use to personalize their experience, grow their success, and prioritize where we invest. The team tackles a diverse set of challenges, such as personalizing onboarding for new retailers, deciding which messages to send and when, and finding the moments that turn a first order with a brand into a lasting relationship. You will work across structured and unstructured data using methods that range from predictive modeling and recommendations to information extraction.
Our team already includes experienced Applied AI/ML Scientists from Uber, Airbnb, Square, Facebook, and Pinterest. Faire will soon be known as a top destination for data scientists and machine learning engineers, and you will help take us there!
What you’ll do
• Own applied ML projects end-to-end: framing the problem, building and shipping the model, and measuring impact.
• Personalize onboarding and the new retailer experience using what we know about each retailer's business.
• Use LLMs to turn unstructured data into signals that improve models and personalization.
• Predict retailer activation, churn, and growth potential to prioritize where we invest.
• Surface the right brands at the right moments to turn first orders into lasting relationships.
• Optimize notifications and brand-to-retailer messaging to drive long-term engagement.
• Use experimentation and causal inference to measure the impact of growth levers, including leading indicators for long-term outcomes like retailer lifetime value.
• Partner across product, engineering, design, marketing, sales, and analytics to turn models into shipped product and business impact.
• Solve challenging problems related to a two-sided marketplace.
Qualifications
• 3+ years of industry experience building and productionizing machine learning models to solve real-world problems (e.g. Sklearn, XGBoost, deep learning)
• Experience with relevant business problems (e-commerce)
• Experience with relevant technical methods (predictive modeling, recommendations and personalization, experimentation and causal inference, LLMs)
• Strong programming skills (Python, SQL)
• An excitement and willingness to learn new tools and techniques
• The ability to independently design and implement ML solutions
• Strong communication skills and the ability to work in a highly cross-functional team
Great to Haves
• Highly recommended: Masters or PhD in Computer Science, Statistics, or related STEM fields.
• Previous experience in marketplace growth, personalization, recommendations, or notification and messaging systems for a two-sided platform.

• Partner with GTM Engineering and Analytics to keep Salesforce and our data foundations clean and reliable, including for AI-powered tools

Fulfilled by Faire (FbF) is one of the biggest bets at Faire. Retailers hold back on shipping cost and per-brand order minimums. Because we hold brand inventory in our own warehouse network, one order can span many brands in a single box, and brands hand off picking, packing, and shipping. Batching also changes the economics: fulfillment and freight costs collapse onto a shared base, so FbF is both a growth engine and a margin lever. It’s a 0-to-1 build that touches nearly every function at Faire, and the operation behind it has to scale.
As Strategy & Operations Senior Lead, Fulfillment, you’ll be the analytical operator at the center of that build. You’ll solve the most complex problems in the operation, remove the process and system bottlenecks that cap throughput, and build the metrics, rhythm, and ways of working that let it scale. You’ll work daily with warehouse operations and partner with Finance, Product, Engineering, and Go-to-Market.
What you’ll do
• Own the most important metrics for the Fulfilled by Faire business by having deep intuition on how they are trending and surfacing the most salient strategic insights to drive them
• Break down complex and ambiguous strategic problems, identify opportunities, develop hypotheses, execute in-depth analyses and make recommendations to Faire’s leadership team
• Lead large cross-functional strategic initiatives that move company metrics in partnership with Product, Sales, Warehouse Ops, Finance, Marketing, etc.
• Own the key fulfillment metrics across service levels, quality, productivity, and cost per order. Define them, build the reporting, and know what is moving them.
• Identify strategic bottlenecks in the systems behind fulfillment, size their impact, and work cross-functionally to unblock them and shape the product roadmap.
• Hold third-party logistics and staffing partners to shared forecasts, plans, and performance targets.

• Provide thought partnership to cross functional teammates to ensure the organization is using data thoughtfully and correctly
