We seek to ignite that passion by setting high standards, championing teamwork, and creating work-life harmony as we collectively navigate rapid growth on a global scale while striving for greater equity and opportunity – inside and outside our organization.
To flourish here, you must be prepared to set a high bar for yourself and those around you. There is always a way to contribute: Acting with autonomy, having accountability and being open to new perspectives are essential to our continued success.
Our deep curiosity to learn and our eagerness to share diverse passions with others gives us balance and injects a one-of-a-kind vibrancy into our culture.
If you are driven to solve exhilarating challenges and have a bias toward action in the face of change, you will be empowered to make a real impact here, with a sharp and passionate team at your back. If Braze sounds like a place where you can thrive, we can’t wait to meet you.
The Role
The best software companies don’t grow through direct sales alone. They grow through ecosystems: networks of partners who extend their reach, deepen customer relationships and deliver outcomes no single company can deliver alone. Technology partners sit closest to the product. They are the platforms, data tools and AI services our customers already use, and how well Braze works with them shapes what customers can build.
Technology partnerships at Braze take three forms. Product partnerships are built into the product, where Braze and a partner’s technology work together for customers. Strategic partnerships are held at a senior level with a small number of platform companies, including the major cloud and large language model providers. And a long tail of ISVs integrate with Braze and extend what customers can do. Each form has grown on its own terms, and the strategy that connects them is still being written.
This role is key to that strategy. Reporting to the AVP, Partner Experience, you own the strategy, program and plan for technology partnerships in all three forms, and you define it in close collaboration with the VP, Technology Partnerships, who leads the strategic relationships. That means deciding what a technology partner is at Braze, what each type gets from us and what we expect back, and how product, strategic and ISV partnerships fit together, so that partners, Product and the field see one ecosystem rather than three separate efforts. This role owns the strategic and program layer that turns that strategy into something partners and internal teams can actually run on.
You will work closely with Product, the Competitive and Monetization Strategy team, Partner Operations and Business Systems, and alongside the Partner Programs Director, whose tiering, benefits, incentives, portal and directory your program runs within. Several parts of the technology program are ready to be rebuilt, including ISV onboarding and evaluation, co-sell and how competitive situations are handled. We need someone who has built a technology partner program before, to decide what stays, what changes and what goes, and to set a plan for the next 24 months.
Salesforce has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Braze. The agreement has not yet closed and remains subject to customary closing conditions. If it completes, there will be work over the next few years to bring the Braze partner program in line with the broader Salesforce partner program and ecosystem, and this role will play an important part in that.
What You’ll Own
• Technology partnerships strategy, program and plan. Own the strategy, program and plan for technology partnerships across product, strategic and ISV partners, including partners that have a commercial motion with Braze and partners that do not. Define the strategy in close collaboration with the VP, Technology Partnerships, so it reflects the strategic relationships they lead as well as the ISVs beyond them, and agree the plan with them before it goes wider. Set out what good looks like, in what order, and who needs to do what.
• What a technology partner is. Draw the line between an ISV partner, which has an integration with Braze, and a technology partner, which has a commercial motion with Braze. The two overlap, but not every ISV has a commercial motion: some bring value through the product alone and help customers reach specific use cases. Define what each gets from Braze and what Braze expects in return, within the tiering, benefits and incentives set by the Partner Programs Director.
• Product partnerships. Bring product partnerships, ISV partnerships and technology partnerships into alignment with Product. Product partnerships are led category by category, so map what exists, agree with the category leads what counts as a partnership, and make sure technology partners have access to, and awareness of, the Product Roadmap.
• The ISV program. Following the defined ISV strategy, rebuild the ISV program: how new ISV partners are evaluated, how they are onboarded, and an ideal partner profile (IPP) that tells the team where to invest. Make onboarding something a partner can complete without chasing, and measure how long it takes for a partner to become active.
• Co-sell and referrals. Own and scale the co-sell program for technology partners. Take an early trial and turn it into a repeatable program, then run it with other partners: how partners are chosen, how opportunities are shared, how it connects with Sales and what we measure. Design a referral program that works in both directions between Braze and technology partners.
• Competitive rules of engagement. Work with the Competitive and Monetization Strategy team to define when a technology partner becomes a competitor and the rules of engagement in those situations. Optimise and scale a universally adopted, ongoing competitive process for technology partners, so that every partnership decision follows the same logic.
• Directory listings outside marketplace. Own Braze listings in other companies’ directories, such as AI-platform directories like Gemini. A customer cannot buy Braze through these listings, which separates them from marketplace work. Work with the Lead Partner Program Manager (Channel & Marketplace) to keep that line clear: if Braze can be bought through it, it belongs to marketplace, and if it is only a listing, it belongs here.
• Evaluating the program. Evaluate the technology partner program and refine the strategy for the next 24 months. Work out where technology partners create value, whether through pipeline from a small number of partners or product adoption across the long tail, and where they do not. Recommend what to keep, stop and start.
• Reporting. Work with Partner Operations and Business Systems to replace separate reports with single views of what is working, such as partner-influenced pipeline, co-sell opportunities, time to activate and customer adoption of integrations.
• Cross-functional alignment. Work with Product, Partner Marketing, Partner PMM, Partner Operations and Business Systems so the program’s rules, tools and messages agree with each other, and bring what you hear from technology partners into the tiering, benefits and incentives that the Partner Programs Director owns.
• Salesforce alignment. If the acquisition completes, lead the work to bring the technology partner program in line with the broader Salesforce partner program and ecosystem.
What This Role Is Really About
Strong partner-influenced pipeline, a co-sell program that repeats, ISVs that onboard quickly and customers who adopt integrations are signs that technology partnerships are working. The strategy sits behind them.
The real work is deciding what technology partnerships are for at Braze, and making sure every form pulls in the same direction. A strategic partnership with a cloud or AI platform, a product partnership built with a category lead and an ISV with a single integration all affect the same customers. When they are planned separately, partners hear different things from different teams and the field cannot tell which partner to bring into a deal. When they share a strategy, a program and a plan, Braze can choose where to invest, say no with a reason and show the value.
You will not manage a team. You will not own the strategic relationships, Product’s roadmap or the competitive strategy, and you will not control the priorities of the people closest to them. The strategy is set together with the VP, Technology Partnerships: they bring the strategic relationships and you bring the program that connects them. Your impact comes from being clear, being right and being someone that Product, the VP, Technology Partnerships and the Partner Experience team want to work with. The best version of this role is a strategist who has built technology partner programs at a larger company, knows which parts of that playbook fit a company our size, and leaves out the rest.
How We Show Up
• Charts strategy across every form. You work with the VP, Technology Partnerships to decide what good looks like for technology partnerships when product, strategic and ISV partnerships have each grown on their own, and you build the model rather than wait for someone else to define it.
• Influences without authority. You don’t own the strategic relationships, Product’s priorities or the competitive strategy, but you shape all three through the quality of your thinking and the trust you build.
• Connects the dots. You see how a partner’s integration, commercial motion, directory listing and place in the Product Roadmap fit together, and you say so clearly.
• Decides with evidence. You work out where technology partners create value and where they don’t, and you stop what isn’t earning its place.
• Right-sizes the program. You know what a mature technology partner program looks like at a larger company. You choose what Braze needs now and show the path to the rest.
• Communicates with impact. You turn a messy cross-functional problem into definitions, rules of engagement and playbooks clear enough that someone else could pick up the work tomorrow.
Who You Are
• 8+ years in technology partnerships, alliances or partner programs at a B2B SaaS or technology company, including having owned the strategy for a technology partner program that spans more than one form, such as product, strategic and ISV partnerships, ideally at a larger or more mature company than Braze
• Has set the strategy and plan for a technology partner program in close partnership with a senior partnerships leader, and can show what changed as a result: who to partner with, who to say no to and where to invest
• Has defined the difference between an integration partner and a partner with a commercial motion, and built the evaluation, onboarding and ideal partner profile that follow from it
• Has taken a co-sell program from a trial to a repeatable program, and understands how referral programs work in both directions
• Has worked with Product teams to bring partner integrations into the roadmap, and can influence how a product team thinks about partners without owning the roadmap
• Has set rules of engagement for competitive situations with technology partners, and made them stick across Sales, Product and Partnerships
• Understands directories and marketplaces and how they differ for technology partners: you know the difference between a listing and a place a customer can buy through
• Comfortable with data: you can build reporting that shows where partners create value, across pipeline influence and customer adoption
• Has a track record of influencing senior stakeholders in Product, Sales and Partnerships without formal authority
• Technically fluent: you can read integration documentation, follow a conversation with engineers and product managers, and judge whether an integration is real
• Prior experience in a MarTech or customer engagement platform business is advantageous, as is familiarity with Salesforce, Crossbeam and Google Workspace
• Based in AMER, with regular working overlap with a manager based in London

THE POSITION
Our roster has an opening with your name on it
FanDuel is looking for a Data Product Manager to join our centralized Data Products team and own the products and services behind how FanDuel personalizes and experiments. Your flagship product is Personalization, one of FanDuel’s largest strategic programs, and it is just getting started.
The vision has two parts. The first is one personalization service that works with any front end. Given a customer, a page, and a moment, it returns ranked content that any surface can render, across sports betting, casino, racing, predictions, fantasy, social and community, payments, editorial, and video. Redesign the app tomorrow and the service does not change. The second is a personalization flywheel. It is a closed loop where ideas are generated, pre-tested, run as live experiments, and analyzed, and each result feeds the next round. Today most good ideas never get tested because experiment capacity is scarce and analysis is slow. You will own the products that change that.
Working closely with the Director of Data Product, you will drive requirements, prioritization, and delivery across customer understanding, ranking, serving, and experimentation. You will partner daily with data science, ML Platform, ML engineering, product analytics, and product managers in every business unit to turn a fast-moving, cross-functional program into shipped, measurable results. This is a high-visibility role tied directly to our “One App, One Customer” data strategy, our 2027 OKRs, and customer engagement, retention, and revenue.
In addition to the specific responsibilities outlined above, employees may be required to perform other such duties as assigned by the Company. This ensures operational flexibility and allows the Company to meet evolving business needs.
THE GAME PLAN
Everyone on our team has a part to play
• Own the backlog and delivery for one personalization product area, such as experimentation tooling or ranking inputs, and deliver it in small, shippable releases.
• Work with the Director of Data Product and senior PMs to shape the personalization roadmap, recommending priorities and trade-offs based on customer data and experiment results.
• Translate broader program goals into clear problem statements, user stories, and acceptance criteria that engineering and data science can plan against.
• Partner with data science and ML engineering on recommendation and ranking approaches, asking questions about accuracy, latency, and cost, and turning their input into product requirements.
• Work with product analytics and the experimentation platform team to define hypotheses, success and guardrail metrics, and test readouts for your area, and share what you learn with the team.
• Support responsible gaming, privacy, and compliance requirements in your area by working with Legal, Compliance, and Responsible Gaming, and escalate open questions early.
• Give status updates to your pod and key stakeholders, flagging risks and blockers early so issues are resolved before they affect delivery.
• Escalate cross-team conflicts and decisions outside your remit to the Director, and bring a recommendation with each escalation.
• Seek and act on feedback from your manager, peers, and partners, and share knowledge with other PMs in the Product Management community.
• Contribute to other Data Product initiatives as priorities evolve, keeping focus on a small number of priorities rather than parallel work.
THE STATS
What we’re looking for in our next teammate
• 3+ years of experience as a Product Manager or Product Owner on personalization, recommendation, search, ranking, experimentation, or other data or ML-powered products, with a record of shipping and measuring results.
• Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field (Computer Science, Engineering, Statistics, Business, or related) or equivalent industry experience. A Master’s degree is a plus.
• Working knowledge of how recommender and ranking systems work (collaborative filtering, learning-to-rank, embeddings, or similar), enough to engage credibly with data scientists and ML engineers on accuracy, latency, and cost.
• Exposure to personalization across varied content types (commerce, media, gaming, social feeds, payments), including cold-start and cross-sell, is a strong plus.
• Hands-on experimentation experience. You have designed and run A/B tests, chosen primary and guardrail metrics, and read results carefully. You know common traps such as peeking, underpowered tests, and novelty effects.
• Hands-on use of AI tools in your product and experimentation work, such as using LLMs to draft hypotheses, design tests, or speed up analysis.
• Working understanding of how LLM-based agents are built and evaluated (tools, prompts, guardrails, and evals). Experience taking an agent into production is a plus.
• Product-led mindset: comfortable questioning engineering-led plans, using frameworks like DACI for decision clarity, and focusing on a small number of priorities.
• Clear communicator who writes crisp requirements, explains trade-offs to technical and non-technical audiences, and is comfortable sizing opportunities in dollar terms.
• SQL proficiency for exploring customer behavior, experiment results, and model performance data.
• Knowledge of sports, gaming, or entertainment, and/or experience in a heavily regulated industry with privacy and responsible-use constraints, is a plus. Familiarity with Databricks, Kafka, Amplitude, Snowplow, or Xtremepush is also a plus.
• Don’t check all the boxes? That’s okay! We encourage you to still apply if you feel like you possess an adjacent skill set and are interested in learning more about this position.
ABOUT FANDUEL
FanDuel Group is the premier mobile gaming company in the United States and Canada. FanDuel Group consists of a portfolio of leading brands across mobile wagering including: America’s #1 Sportsbook, FanDuel Sportsbook; its leading iGaming platform, FanDuel Casino; the industry’s unquestioned leader in horse racing and advance-deposit wagering, FanDuel Racing; and its daily fantasy sports product.
In addition, FanDuel Group operates FanDuel TV, its broadly distributed linear cable television network and FanDuel TV+, its leading direct-to-consumer OTT platform. FanDuel Group has a presence across all 50 states, Canada, and Puerto Rico.
The company is based in New York with US offices in Los Angeles, Atlanta, and Jersey City, as well as global offices in Canada and Scotland. The company’s affiliates have offices worldwide, including in Ireland, Portugal, Romania, and Australia.

1 in 4 people in the US have a treatable mental health condition, but most providers don't accept insurance, making therapy too expensive for most people. Headway’s mission is to fix this by building a new mental healthcare system everyone can access. We started by solving the biggest barrier to care: insurance. The admin work - credentialing, claims, payment reconciliation - is a nightmare. We've automated that.



But we're going further. Over 90,000 providers across all 50 states run their practice on our software, serving over 2.6 million patients. We are building the best tools for therapists to run their entire practice, reimagining the experience of finding a therapist, and investing in the platform foundations to enable this at scale, and building much of it with AI. We aren't just a billing layer; we are becoming the platform where care actually happens.



We're a Series D company with $325M+ in funding (a16z, Accel, Spark Capital, etc.), looking for exceptional people to help us achieve this mission. We want your time here to be the most meaningful experience of your career. Join us, and help change mental healthcare for the better.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Senior Associate on Headway’s Payer team, you’ll be the engine behind our health plan partnerships, owning critical workstreams end-to-end. Depending on the role track, you’ll own payer-facing work, such as market and buyer analysis, deal content, executive briefings, and recurring touchpoints with payer counterparts, or power the commercial operating system behind it, including KPI and competitive intelligence, reporting cycles, and enablement. You’ll do this as part of one of the most AI-forward commercial teams in digital health, where we expect you to direct the tools, question their output, and own every recommendation that carries your name.




YOU WILL

 - Research payers and buyers, including their network gaps, member demand, decision-makers, and the fewest moves to a win, and turn that into account plans

 - Build pitch decks, executive briefings, and meeting prep that move deals forward

 - Own defined payer touchpoints, such as working sessions and follow-ups, and track every open action to close

 - Track plan health on assigned plans (enrollment, claims performance, SLA adherence), and drive operational issues to resolution with Ops, Provider Network, and Finance

 - Project-manage pieces of launches and special projects, including timelines, owners, and readiness checklists

 - Run our intelligence and reporting cadence: dashboards, rate audits, competitive benchmarking, and enablement materials


YOU’D BE A GREAT FIT IF

 - You have 2–4+ years in consulting, business development, partnerships, sales, or strategy & ops, where you owned complex problems or external relationships end-to-end. Healthcare experience is a bonus.

 - You have genuine commercial instinct. You read rooms, build trust quickly, and move conversations toward outcomes.

 - You’re operationally excellent. The trains always run on time, and you manage a huge volume of moving pieces without dropping any.

 - You’re resourceful and scrappy, and you leave no stone unturned.

 - You use AI tools fluently and skeptically. You know what they’re good at and where they fail, and you never ship an output you haven’t pressure-tested.

 - You seek an environment that fosters individual growth through open feedback and high autonomy

 - You’re motivated to take on one of our generation’s defining problems: access to mental healthcare

Medical, dental, vision, HSA/FSA, 401(k) including match for 2027!, Carrot Fertility reimbursement, and paid parental, medical and caregiver leave.

Veeva’s Solution Consultants are an integral part of our sales team, supporting our Strategists and Account Partners as technical product experts in the sales cycle, proving both the fit and value of our products to our customers.  You will work closely with our Strategy, Sales, Product Management, and Consulting teams to sell Veeva Vault, our cloud-based content and data management software. About Outreach
Outreach is a leading agentic AI platform built for revenue teams. Outreach lets revenue leaders hireAI agents that act rather than advise, working as true teammates that expand capacity and embed the skills of top sellers across every go-to-market workflow, from prospecting and engaging accounts to managing deals, coaching reps, forecasting, and retaining and expanding existing accounts. By unifying sales engagement, conversation intelligence, and revenue intelligence in a single connected platform, Outreach gives revenue leaders full-funnel visibility, greater forecast confidence, and more pipeline without adding headcount. World-leading enterprise organizations, including Databricks, SAP, and Siemens, rely on Outreach to power their revenue teams. To learn more, visit www.outreach.ai.

Managed Services sits within Professional Services. We're Outreach, CRM, and GTM technology experts who help customers get full value from the platform once implementation ends. We are trusted advisors that drive adoption, flag risk, and grow usage, so customers keep exceeding their goals.

You'll join our FDE, Managed Services team, chartered with building our customers' AI Agents beyond what was set up during implementation: opening new use cases and growing Amplify credit and product consumption.

You will partner with the leaders and team to set the technical standard for the practice and be a go-to resource when other consultants hit edge cases. You'll stay technically fluent in Outreach's evolving capabilities, AI included, so you can configure and troubleshoot in real time. 
The role mixes technology and business consulting with solution design and project management. You'll work closely with Customer Success and Account Executives, build rapport fast, and influence customer outcomes.

Founded in 1998, Gracenote is one of America’s most iconic and respected media companies.
 
We are seeking a technical, customer-focused Product Solutions Architect to lead customer technical pre-sales and implementation for our suite of metadata products and AI products, including the Gracenote Model Context Protocol (MCP) Servers. You will serve as the primary technical subject matter expert for the Gracenote suite of products, enabling B2B clients to successfully integrate our authoritative metadata into their discovery experience including AI-powered integrations. You will lead the end-to-end customer technical engagement lifecycle of technical solutions, from pre-sales consultation, requirements gathering, product solutioning and  proof-of-concept development to post-implementation support and strategic product advocacy.

Title and Summary
The Customer Success Operations – Platform & Reporting role owns and advances the Loyalty Gainsight deployment and the reporting infrastructure that enables Customer Success teams to operate with consistent data, workflows, and executive-ready insights. This role translates business requirements into scalable platform capabilities, dashboards, KPIs, and operating routines that help teams understand customer health, risk, adoption, outcomes, and value realization.
Overview
Services within Mastercard is responsible for acquiring, engaging, and retaining customers by managing fraud and risk, enhancing cybersecurity, and improving the digital payments experience. We provide value-added services and leverage expertise, data-driven insights, and execution.
Our Customer Success teams play a crucial role in ensuring customers achieve their desired outcomes while maximizing the value of Mastercard’s products and services. The team supports onboarding, ongoing strategic engagement, customer feedback, product improvement, customer satisfaction, retention, advocacy, and value expansion.
Role
Are you passionate about building scalable platforms, reporting, and operational infrastructure that help customer-facing teams deliver consistent, high-impact customer experiences? Join Mastercard’s Services Customer Success team as a Customer Success Operations Senior Specialist focused on Platform & Reporting.
Platform Ownership & Gainsight Deployment
• Own the Loyalty Gainsight deployment roadmap, including configuration, enhancement prioritization, adoption, and ongoing optimization.
• Partner with Customer Success, Product, Program, and Regional teams to translate operating needs into scalable Gainsight workflows, playbooks, health scores, customer segmentation, and engagement models.
• Ensure Gainsight supports scaled, offline and digital Customer Success motions through integrated workflows and streamlined user experiences.
• Serve as a platform subject-matter expert for Customer Success users, helping teams adopt consistent processes and maximize the value of the CS technology stack.
Reporting, Metrics & Insights
• Design and maintain reporting, dashboards, and measurement frameworks using Gainsight and other tools.
• Define and track KPIs that measure Customer Success performance, customer health, engagement, risk, adoption, value realization, and operational execution.
• Build reporting views for executives, regional leaders, Program teams, Product teams, and front-line Customer Success colleagues.
• Identify leading indicators of positive outcomes, risks, and trends that enable proactive action and continuous improvement.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
• Collect user feedback, prioritize enhancements, and partner with technical and business stakeholders to improve platform adoption and usability.
• Champion platform-enabled best practices across the organization and support change-management activities tied to new workflows, dashboards, and tools.
• Support communication, training, and enablement needed to drive adoption of Gainsight and related reporting capabilities.
All About You
• Experience in Customer Success Operations, Sales Operations, Business Operations, Delivery Excellence, or related operational roles.
• Strong knowledge of Gainsight or similar Customer Success platforms; hands-on experience with configuration, reporting, workflows, health scores, or playbooks preferred.
• Experience building reporting, dashboards, KPI frameworks, and measurement models using tools such as Gainsight, Salesforce, Tableau, Power BI, Excel, or similar platforms.
• Strong analytical skills with the ability to translate data into clear insights, executive-ready narratives, and actionable recommendations.
• Proven ability to translate business requirements into scalable platform capabilities and operational processes.
• Ability to work globally and cross-functionally, influencing stakeholders and driving alignment across teams.
• Strong ownership mindset, deep sense of curiosity, continuous-improvement orientation, and ability to manage multiple priorities in a growing global organization.
• Experience supporting adoption of new processes, technologies, and organizational changes.
• Passion for delivering customer value and enabling customer-facing teams through scalable systems, insights, and operational excellence.

Role summary
DT is in continuous transformation that impacts how 1,100+ people power the company, grow and thrive.  This role is the connective tissue that keeps that transformation coherent and make sure the people side of DT moves as fast as the technology side.  It builds the strategic muscle DT already has on financial planning and applies it to how DT operates, how its managers grow, and how its people experience change.
Scope of impact
Enterprise level. This role connects and operates across the full extended management team (DT ELT, including DTLT and their direct reports). It drives momentum for transformation work happening across every DT sub-function, represents DT’s workforce needs directly to HR leadership, and holds the connective view that keeps management development and engagement work grounded in what’s happening in the organization.
The six scope pillars
• Curate, activate and maintain the health of the DT operating model : owns the ongoing evolution of DT’s operating model as a living strategic asset rather than a periodic deliverable. Drives the conversations that keep DT’s structure, ways of working, and talent strategy ahead of where the business is going, anticipating the organizational implications of AI, human-machine teaming, and the continued compression of the line between technology delivery and business execution.
• DTLT and extended management team maturity : in partnership with GP (HRBP, GLD, and more), designs and runs programs that close the gap between what DTLT commits to at the strategy table and what managers and teams do in the field.
• Transformation intelligence and translation : maintains a live, interpreted view of every active transformation across DT and translates what’s changing into what managers and individual contributors need to do differently.
• HR representation for DT : acts as DT’s “business” voice into HR. Defines what programs, policies, and support DT needs based on its operating model and transformation portfolio, and ensures they are both operational and effective. Strategic guide to lead HR partnership.
• Culture and employee engagement strategy : owns recognition, town halls, and events as tools that reinforce the operating model and culture shift, not as standalone activities.
• Communications as output : uses communications to activate and align people around the five pillars above.
Key responsibilities
Curate, activate and maintain the health of the DT operating model
• Own DT’s operating model as a living document: maintain it, pressure-test it against what’s happening in the organization, and drive the leadership conversations that evolve it.
• Anticipate the organizational implications of evolving technologies and external market shifts. Bring those implications into DT’s planning conversations before they become reactive ones.
• Partner with Strategy and Operations to ensure the operating model is reflected in AOP design, OKR construction, and workforce planning, not treated as a separate workstream.
DTLT and extended management team maturity
• In partnership with GP, HRBP, GLD, and others, design and run management development programs that build durable capability, not episodic event exposure, for DTLT and their full set of directs.
• In partnership with HR, define what management maturity means specifically in DT’s context: the behaviors, judgment patterns, and operating norms our operating model calls for, not a generic framework imported from elsewhere.
• Close the gap between what DTLT commits to at the strategy table and what managers and supervisors execute in the field, diagnosing where that gap lives and building programs that address the root cause.
• Hold HR and GLD accountable to DT’s requirements rather than accepting standard offerings. This role sets the agenda for that partnership.
Transformation intelligence and translation
• Maintain a current, interpreted view of every active transformation across DT. This is not a status tracker but an organizational read that informs what leaders need to know and do.
• Translate what’s changing across DT into specific behavior changes for managers and ICs, naming those behaviors explicitly rather than communicating at the level of themes or priorities.
• Advise DTLT on where transformation fatigue, change saturation, or misalignment between parallel workstreams is creating risk, before it surfaces as an engagement or performance problem.
• Keep management development and culture activation work calibrated to real transformation conditions rather than a generic calendar.
HR representation for DT
• Act as DT’s requirements owner with HR, defining what DT needs from programs, policies, and support based on its operating model and transformation portfolio, not reacting to what HR proposes.
• Identify gaps between what HR offers and what DT’s operating rhythm actually demands, and close those gaps by specifying requirements clearly enough that HR can act on them.
• Own the DT-HR partnership cadence so it runs on DT’s planning cycle, ensuring HR programs land when DT needs them, not when HR schedules them.
• Represent DT’s workforce needs at the HR leadership level with enough authority and context to influence program design, not just adoption.
Culture and employee engagement strategy
• Own recognition programs, town halls, and events, and connect each to a specific culture or operating model goal.
• Use communications to build alignment around the operating model and management priorities, positioning communications as a delivery mechanism.
What this role is not
• A communications role that occasionally touches strategy.
• An HR/GLD liaison who accepts standard offerings and schedules them for DT.
• A calendar owner for events and town halls with no explicit tie to DT’s operating model or culture goals.
• A PMO function that tracks transformation data without interpreting it or translating it into action.
• A role that waits for the operating model to be handed to it. This person shapes it.
• A support function to DTLT. A strategic partner to it.
This role requires someone who has done the hard version of each of these things, not someone who has been adjacent to them.
• Has owned an operating model evolution in a large, matrixed technology organization, not as a consultant who recommended changes, but as the person accountable for making them stick.
• Can read an organization: walk into a management team, identify where the stated operating model and the lived operating model diverge, and name the gap without waiting to be told.
• Has designed and run management development programs for VP and SVP-level audiences, starting from a diagnosis of what capability actually needs to change.
• Has operated with genuine authority at the VP and SVP level, shaping decisions and preparing materials for others to decide with.
• Has built something from scratch in a matrixed environment without a fully defined mandate, pre-cleared budget, or stable organizational context.
• Has held an HR partnership with enough confidence to define requirements rather than accept offerings, and has the organizational credibility to make that posture land.
• Understands the organizational implications of AI-driven work transformation, not at the level of talking points, but well enough to advise senior leaders on what it means for structure, roles, and capability development.
• Has managed parallel, evolving transformation workstreams simultaneously, and has demonstrated the judgment to know when to push and when to pause.
• Communicates at the executive level as a native capability, not as a skill they apply when needed, but as the default mode they operate in.

The Company
PayPal has been revolutionizing commerce globally for more than 25 years. Creating innovative experiences that make moving money, selling, and shopping simple, personalized, and secure, PayPal empowers consumers and businesses in approximately 200 markets to join and thrive in the global economy.
We operate a global, two-sided network at scale that connects hundreds of millions of merchants and consumers. We help merchants and consumers connect, transact, and complete payments, whether they are online or in person. PayPal is more than a connection to third-party payment networks. We provide proprietary payment solutions accepted by merchants that enable the completion of payments on our platform on behalf of our customers.
We offer our customers the flexibility to use their accounts to purchase and receive payments for goods and services, as well as the ability to transfer and withdraw funds. We enable consumers to exchange funds more safely with merchants using a variety of funding sources, which may include a bank account, a PayPal or Venmo account balance, PayPal and Venmo branded credit products, a credit card, a debit card, certain cryptocurrencies, or other stored value products such as gift cards, and eligible credit card rewards. Our PayPal, Venmo, and Xoom products also make it safer and simpler for friends and family to transfer funds to each other. We offer merchants an end-to-end payments solution that provides authorization and settlement capabilities, as well as instant access to funds and payouts. We also help merchants connect with their customers, process exchanges and returns, and manage risk. We enable consumers to engage in cross-border shopping and merchants to extend their global reach while reducing the complexity and friction involved in enabling cross-border trade.
Our beliefs are the foundation for how we conduct business every day. We live each day guided by our core values of Inclusion, Innovation, Collaboration, and Wellness. Together, our values ensure that we work together as one global team with our customers at the center of everything we do – and they push us to ensure we take care of ourselves, each other, and our communities.

Job Summary:
The Manager, Software Engineering owns PayPal’s ServiceNow IT Asset Management (ITAM) product suite: its roadmap, backlog, and outcomes across hardware assets, software assets, and the procurement flows that feed them.
The role leads through programs and resources, not direct reports. It sets product direction and acceptance standards, and directs the engineers, vendors, and partners who build and run the product, staying accountable for their quality, security, and audit readiness.
Scope covers Hardware Asset Management, Software Asset Management, and integrations with Ariba, SAP, the CMDB, and supply-chain partners. The goal is zero-touch asset operations: self-fulfilling requests, accurate records, and supervised AI agents for routine tasks.
The role prioritizes ITAM work, anticipates risks, and advises colleagues on ServiceNow ITAM. It keeps roadmap, demand, and benefits traceable in ServiceNow SPM and Jira for planning, governance, and delivery.
Job Description:
Essential Responsibilities:
• Directly manages software development projects (including program management) and execution through individual contributors. May also lead project teams across platforms or groups
• Implements processes to drive strong operational hygiene for all components and systems within their group
• Responsible for the delivery of projects, including quality and timeliness, that impact their domain and potentially one other
• Demonstrates strong tactical ability by managing the roadmap for a scrum team responsible for technical issues of diverse scope where analysis requires an understanding of current business or tends
• Competent at communicating technical issues with non-technical audiences
• Analyzes multiple sources of information and identifies & resolves complex technical, operational, and organizational problems relating to software development.
• Collaborates with direct team, managers in org, stakeholders such as Product Owners & PMO
Minimum Qualifications:
• 5+ years relevant experience and a Bachelor’s degree OR Any equivalent combination of education and experience.
Additional Responsibilities & Preferred Qualifications :
ServiceNow Responsibilities
• Product vision & roadmap — Own the ServiceNow ITAM product vision and multi-quarter roadmap across HAM, SAM, and asset procurement, aligned with the Autonomous Operations strategy and the annual planning cycle.
• Backlog ownership & prioritization — Own and prioritize a single ITAM backlog in Jira; write and refine epics and user stories with clear acceptance criteria; make the trade-off calls; and retire stale or duplicate demand so the backlog reflects real, funded work.
• Zero Touch Request & supply-chain integration — Lead delivery of Zero Touch Request with CDW, including the ServiceNow-to-CDW integrations, so that approved device requests move to fulfillment, shipping, and receipt without manual handling.
• Hardware Asset Management — Drive the hardware lifecycle in ServiceNow from request and receipt through deployment, refresh, reclamation, and disposal, including the disposal hand-off to Finance fixed-asset records.
• Software Asset Management — Lead the ServiceNow Software Asset Management Professional build-out with the SAM process owners: contracts and entitlements, license allocation and reclamation, software normalization, and compliance positions for priority publishers.
• Procurement & finance interlocks — Define requirements for the integrations between ServiceNow, Ariba, and SAP so that purchase requests, purchase orders, receipts, and asset records reconcile, and partner with Finance on cost-center, capitalization, and disposal requirements.
• Asset data quality & CSDM alignment — Set and measure asset-data quality standards (completeness, ownership, accuracy, and asset-to-configuration item (CI) reconciliation) with the ITOM and CMDB architects, aligned to the Common Service Data Model.
• AI-assisted asset operations — Identify and deliver AI-assisted and agentic workflows for routine asset work, such as request triage, license reclamation, and data-quality remediation, with human supervision, traceability, and audit controls designed in.
• Delivery oversight of contingent-worker & vendor teams — Direct the contingent-worker engineers and vendor partners who build ITAM capabilities: set acceptance criteria and definitions of done, review output for quality and platform fit, and hold delivery to its commitments.
• Stakeholder design & platform guardrails — Run design sessions with asset, procurement, finance, information security, and operations stakeholders to meet business requirements while protecting the platform from technical debt and unnecessary customization.
• Outcome metrics & reporting — Define and report ITAM product outcomes, such as request-to-fulfillment cycle time, touchless fulfillment rate, asset-record accuracy, license compliance, and reclaimed spend, to Autonomous Operations and ESET leadership.
• Audit & control readiness — Represent the ITAM product in internal and external audits, keep asset and license records audit-ready, and support capitalization and benefits tracking for ITAM investments.
• Advising & capability building — Advise colleagues on ServiceNow ITAM capabilities, and coach analysts, engineers, and contingent workers on product practices to build lasting capability in the organization.
Expected Qualifications
• Proven experience as a product manager or product owner for ServiceNow IT Asset Management (HAM, SAM Professional, or both) in an enterprise environment
• Experience owning a backlog end to end: writing epics and user stories with acceptance criteria, prioritizing against capacity, and running agile ceremonies in Jira or a similar tool
• Experience directing delivery by engineers, managed-service teams, or vendor teams, including setting acceptance criteria and holding partners to quality and timeliness
• Working knowledge of the ServiceNow asset and CMDB data model, including asset-to-CI relationships and the Common Service Data Model
• Experience defining requirements for integrations between ServiceNow and procurement, finance, or supplier systems (e.g., Ariba, SAP, reseller or original equipment manufacturer (OEM) APIs) using REST, IntegrationHub, or similar
• Working knowledge of the hardware asset lifecycle and of software licensing and compliance (e.g., publisher license models, entitlements, and true-ups)
• Experience defining product outcome metrics and reporting them to senior leaders
• Strong written and verbal communication, including explaining technical trade-offs to finance, procurement, and executive audiences
• Ability to lead cross-functional work and influence partners without formal reporting authority
Additional Responsibilities & Preferred Qualifications
• ServiceNow Certified Implementation Specialist (CIS) in Hardware Asset Management or Software Asset Management; ServiceNow Certified System Administrator (CSA)
• Experience delivering zero-touch or automated device provisioning with a hardware reseller or OEM
• Experience applying AI or agentic automation (e.g., ServiceNow Now Assist or AI Agents) to asset or service-management workflows
• Product or asset-management certification, such as Certified Scrum Product Owner (CSPO), Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe) Product Owner/Product Manager, or an International Association of IT Asset Managers (IAITAM) credential

About this role
Your Team:
Aladdin Data brings together product, data, technology, and domain expertise to build foundational data capabilities that support users and business workflows. This role sits within the Data Foundation Layer and focuses on the Client Book of Record (CBOR), helping evolve a trusted, governed data foundation that supports consistent client and relationship data across the enterprise.
You will work closely with engineering, data science, architecture, data governance, and business teams to expand the foundation beyond structured data and make high-value unstructured information accessible for analytics, artificial intelligence, and next-generation product experiences.
Your Role and Impact:
As a Data Product Solutions Lead , you will lead the product direction and delivery of the unstructured data foundation for CBOR , establishing how unstructured enterprise information is ingested, organized, governed, retrieved, and activated alongside structured client data. You will develop the roadmap for this capability and translate business needs into scalable product requirements and solutions, balancing data quality, governance, usability, technical feasibility, and measurable business value.
You will operate at the intersection of product management, data platforms, and artificial intelligence (AI). You will establish the data capabilities needed for retrieval, grounding, semantic understanding, and AI-powered experiences while partnering with engineering and architecture on the underlying technical design.
You will develop a strong understanding of data pipelines, application programming interfaces (APIs), metadata, retrieval approaches, AI models and agents, and structured and unstructured data patterns to make informed product decisions without being expected to serve as the primary engineer. You will also define measures of success and use adoption, quality, evaluation, and user feedback to continuously improve the foundation as data, technology, and business needs evolve.
Your Responsibilities:
In every role at BlackRock, you'll be expected to apply sound judgement and critical thinking to solve complex problems, adapt as the business evolves, and combine the curiosity to explore new approaches and technologies with the rigor to challenge the results. The scope of this role also includes the following responsibilities:
• Define and drive the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for CBOR's unstructured data foundation , translating enterprise data and AI needs into clear product outcomes and scalable capabilities.
• Own product requirements and prioritization across ingestion, enrichment, metadata, retrieval, access, governance, and consumption capabilities, balancing foundational investments with near-term business value.
• Translate business and user needs into technical data-product requirements , partnering with engineering, architecture, data science, and governance teams on data patterns, integrations, APIs, semantic models, and platform capabilities.
• Shape AI-ready data capabilities that enable knowledge retrieval, grounding, semantic understanding, generative AI, AI agents, and agentic workflows, connecting trusted structured and unstructured information to user experiences and business processes.
• Partner on data quality, governance, security, privacy, access controls, lineage, and responsible AI requirements , helping ensure unstructured information can be used appropriately and reliably in production data and AI solutions.
• Define success measures and evaluation approaches using data-quality measures, retrieval and AI evaluation, telemetry, experimentation, adoption, user feedback, and business outcomes to continuously improve the platform.
• Evaluate evolving data and AI capabilities and build AI-powered tooling that streamlines product solutioning , accelerating how the team explores use cases, translates business needs into solution concepts and requirements, evaluates options, and develops scalable data and AI solutions while grounding recommendations in user needs, architecture, governance, risk, and measurable business value.
Your Experience:
• Demonstrated product management or product ownership experience working with data platforms, enterprise technology, analytics, or related digital products, including developing roadmaps, setting priorities, translating business needs into product requirements, and partnering with technical teams to deliver outcomes.
• Experience with enterprise data platforms and data-management concepts , including ingestion, data modeling, metadata, data quality, governance, and consumption patterns; exposure to Snowflake, Azure SQL Server, or comparable enterprise data environments is valuable.
• Understanding of structured and unstructured data approaches and familiarity with concepts such as semantic data models, knowledge retrieval, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), grounding, search, and preparing enterprise data for AI use cases.
• Working knowledge of AI and machine learning product concepts , including generative AI, large language models, AI agents and agentic workflows, context management, prompting, evaluation, and the opportunities and limitations of AI-powered products.
• Experience partnering with technical teams on platform and solution design , including data pipelines, APIs, system integrations, orchestration, and architectural trade-offs, with the ability to shape solutions without being the primary engineer implementing them.
• Strong analytical and product judgment , with experience using metrics, evaluation, experimentation, quantitative insights, and qualitative user feedback to prioritize work, assess product quality, and improve outcomes.
• Ability to work across engineering, data science, architecture, data governance, and business teams , communicate complex concepts clearly, navigate ambiguity, manage multiple priorities, and build alignment around product decisions.

Who We’re Looking For
We are seeking an Associate Technical Product Manager to lead roadmap execution for foundational user interface capabilities within the Charles River and Alpha Platforms.
This role is ideal for a product professional with 4+ years of technical product management experience who is highly technical, curious, and comfortable using modern tools to solve problems independently. We are looking for someone fluent in generative AI tools, modern web technologies, APIs, data, and user experience, and who naturally looks for faster and better ways to get work done.
You do not need to be a software engineer, but you should be comfortable working with technology directly. For example, rather than defaulting to a PowerPoint presentation, you might use AI-assisted tools to quickly create a more compelling interactive presentation. Rather than requesting a new report, you might use an available API and tools such as VS Code and GitHub Copilot to prototype a simple web application that answers the question. Rather than manually analyzing a large set of product feedback, you might use an LLM to help identify themes and then validate the results yourself.
We are looking for someone who combines this builder mindset with strong product judgment, an understanding of user experience, and the ability to lead product discovery and execution in a complex enterprise environment.
Why This Role Is Important to Us
You will join the Platform UI Framework team within the Charles River Investment Management Solution (CRIMS), a market-leading SaaS platform that powers front-to-back investment workflows for some of the world’s largest financial institutions.
As we scale our platform, your talent will be critical in evolving our foundational UI capabilities, improving developer and user experiences, and enabling rapid innovation across the organization. Your ability to combine product leadership with practical technical fluency will help the team investigate product questions, communicate ideas, and validate solutions more quickly.
What You Will Be Responsible For
• Collect and refine business and functional requirements from clients, engineering, architecture, security, operations, and other stakeholders, ensuring platform capabilities meet user, performance, scalability, security, and compliance needs.

• Partner with UX designers and engineers to create experiences that are intuitive, efficient, accessible, consistent, and technically achievable.

• Create lightweight prototypes, scripts, visualizations, or web applications when a tangible artifact will produce better insight or stakeholder feedback than a traditional document or presentation.
• Promote a smooth developer experience by helping ensure platform services, components, documentation, and workflows are understandable and intuitive.
• Use product analytics, user feedback, and direct stakeholder engagement to understand adoption, identify friction, and shape roadmap priorities.
• Become a subject matter expert in the coverage area and provide informed recommendations that help shape product strategy and growth.
• Support sales, professional services, and client support activities to improve the client experience and inform future product investments.
Qualifications
• 4+ years of experience in technical product management, business analysis, platform engineering, UX, software development, or a related technology role within a SaaS or enterprise software environment.
• Strong understanding of product management practices, including discovery, requirements definition, user stories, prioritization, roadmaps, iterative delivery, and stakeholder management.
• Strong interest in user experience and interaction design, with the ability to understand complex workflows and identify opportunities to simplify them.
• Technical fluency with modern web applications, including familiarity with React, JavaScript or TypeScript, REST APIs, JSON, authentication, web services, and cloud-based applications.
• Demonstrated ability to use generative AI and AI-assisted tools as part of everyday work, including research, analysis, prototyping, communication, coding, and problem solving.
• Comfort using tools such as VS Code, GitHub, GitHub Copilot, command-line utilities, APIs, and browser developer tools to explore ideas and solve problems independently.
• Ability to create lightweight prototypes, scripts, visualizations, or web applications to explore a product idea or answer a business question. Production-level software engineering experience is not required.
• Comfort working with data and selecting the right tool for the problem, whether Excel, SQL, an API, Power BI, or a lightweight custom application.
• Proven ability to work with cross-functional teams to deliver scalable, secure, and high-impact platform capabilities.
• Strong technical acumen and the ability to engage meaningfully with engineers, architects, designers, security teams, and non-technical stakeholders.
• Experience with Azure cloud services and enterprise security or compliance requirements is beneficial.
• Experience with Jira, Confluence, Figma, GitHub, or similar product development tools is beneficial.
• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Human-Computer Interaction, Product Design, Business, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
• Experience in financial services, enterprise SaaS, or another regulated industry is a plus.

Manager, Product Manager - Fraud Decisioning
At Capital One, we believe great products begin with a deep understanding of our customers. From our earliest days, we pioneered the use of predictive modeling to individually personalize credit card offers, turning the entire industry on its head. As we’ve grown bigger, we’ve found more and more ways to use technology and face-to-face conversations to understand the human problems associated with money and finances.
In the Consumer Bank, we’ve combined this human-centered approach with our heritage of data-driven decision making to design, build and test our way to truly enabling financial experiences. We’ve challenged ourselves to spend less time planning, more time doing, and, above all else, to see the world through the eyes of our customers as they work to understand and manage their money.
Are you passionate about improving the way people interact with their money? Are you driven by the delight you bring to customers? Do you keep asking, “why,” until you hit the root? It’s common to fall in love with solutions, but have you ever fallen in love with the problem? Do you have an opinion on whether shipping is more important than perfection? Do you have a healthy dose of skepticism for the impossible? If you’re nodding your head, then we want you!
About the Team
At the heart of any bank account, customers move and manage their money—transferring money between their accounts, wiring money to purchase a home, and more. At the same time, bad actors are constantly evolving to scam or steal from our customers. Our mission is twofold: make it seamless for good customers to use their account day in, day out, while making it impossible for those bad actors to get in.
To accomplish this, we build the intelligent data-driven brain behind those customer experiences, managing the policies, models, and data integrations that power our automated decisions. We also design empathetic, trust-building experiences for customers and associates when a decision requires a human touch. We are a team of strategists, builders, and customer advocates who thrive on solving complex problems at the intersection of technology, data, and human experience.
Role Overview
We're looking for a Product Manager focused on Fraud Decisioning — a role at the heart of Capital One's mission to Change Banking for Good. In this role, you will lead the strategy and implementation for detecting and mitigating complex threats across customer experiences, including Account Takeover (ATO) and emerging scam vectors. You will oversee automated and risk-informed decisioning for money movement across key payment rails; balancing real-time fraud protection and loss coverage against customer friction and financial inclusion. Partnering closely with Data Science, Tech, Operations, and Business Analysts, you will drive the next generation of intelligent decisioning systems that safeguard millions of customer transactions every day.
On any given day in the Bank you’ll be:
• Empowered. Part of a team driving the bank’s omni-channel acquisitions strategy responsible for setting and delivering the decisioning and treatment framework to ensure our business is gaining profitable customers through both digital and digital-human interactions
• Learning constantly. Work deeply with customers, frontline associates, designers, technologists, analysts, marketers and data scientists to build cutting edge solutions
• Innovating relentlessly. Pushing big change by asking bold questions; starting small, testing, and learning your way to something dramatically better
• Sharing openly. Telling stories that change the way people think about building products and solving problems, and that illustrate the power of what software can do to make them even better
• Connecting creatively. Jump-starting a self-supporting community by sowing the right seeds, building the right tools, integrating the right off-the-shelf products, and just plain elbow grease
• Succeeding strategically. Solving the right problem and holding on the wrong one.

Sr. Business Manager - Bank Fraud Defense
Summary: As a Senior Manager, Business Analysis at Capital One, you will apply your strategic and analytical skills to major company challenges. You will lead and team with world-class professionals to develop and test strategies that ultimately impact the bottom line. And you'll do it all in a collaborative environment that values your insight, encourages you to take on new responsibility, promotes continuous learning, and rewards innovation.
There is no shortage of appetite or creativity for deposit fraud, with ~$500M in annual attempts and losses exceeding $20M. As bad actors get smarter and upskill with AI tools, we are looking for a tenacious Senior Manager to lead the fight for the good side. This is a dynamic, high-impact space where your decisions will directly impact customer trust and operational resilience. In this role, you’ll own the P&L for the space, guiding your team through day-to-day threat mitigation while maintaining a strategic lens to help drive our long-term investment agenda. Partnering closely with product, tech, data science, and operations teams, you’ll keep fraudsters at bay while enabling the bank to scale toward our 20M PBR goals.
General Responsibilities:
• Strategic leadership: Develop business strategies that will drive growth, profitability, and competitive success for Capital One in the face of shifting consumer and regulatory behavior
• Business ownership: Have an ownership mindset, and potentially P&L accountability for a business segment. Strategic planning with a 1-6 month horizon
• Leadership: May manage and develop a team of analysts. Coaching and mentoring associates throughout the organization with a goal of developing and retaining talent at Capital One
• Product: Develop and implement new product and pricing strategies for various lending products; lead product level modeling/analytics
• Marketing: Lead direct to consumer marketing efforts for select products, and strategic intent for products distributed through various channels. Build targeted insights to inform the design and development of new customer experiences, as well as breakthrough technology and concepts designed to deliver on new go-to-market strategies
• Credit Risk: Drive step-change improvements in credit performance by connecting drivers of future consumer credit trends to historical behavior, creating risk models, and testing hypotheses using rigorous monitoring and analysis
• Execution: Coordinate across the line of business to manage and sequence delivery of business intent, build business requirements and execute against the product strategy. Oversee multiple projects and programs concurrently
• Partnership: Work closely with colleagues across Capital One including: IT, Sales, Operations, Finance and others to drive improvement in quality, volume, service, and profitability
• Strategic & analytic orientation: A proven track record of decision making and problem solving based on analytics. Conceptual thinking skills must be complemented by a strong quantitative orientation, given that a large part of the business is based on rigorous analytic marketing & credit risk management
• Strong business judgment, leadership and integrity: He/she should be a tenacious decision maker, able to bring a healthy, aggressive, yet responsible approach to business
• Solid people leadership experience: Ability to build and leverage the capabilities of a high-performing team, as well as business partners across the enterprise. He/she should foster innovation, drive critical decisions, hold business partners accountable, and be able to consistently deliver results
• Strong executive communication skills: Impeccable written and oral communication credentials, coupled with strategic influencing skills and the ability to drive agreement through intellect, interpersonal and negotiation skills
• Clear results orientation: display an intense focus on achieving both short and long term goals. He/she should be able to drive and execute an agenda in an uncertain and fluid environment
• Successful track record of thriving in a fast paced, entrepreneurial and dynamic environment. Previous consulting experience is a plus

• 2+ years of experience in product development

Senior Associate, Product Manager - Capital One Travel
As a Senior Associate, Product Manager in Capital One Travel, you will own the strategy, roadmap, and end-to-end execution of high-impact customer experiences across web and mobile. Operating at the intersection of fintech, e-commerce, and hospitality, you will partner closely with engineering, design, data science, and external travel suppliers to build intuitive, high-converting products that deepen cardholder loyalty.
Key Responsibilities
• Product Strategy & Vision: Define and evangelize a compelling product vision and multi-quarter roadmap aligned with broader Capital One Travel and cardholder engagement goals.
• End-to-End Execution: Lead cross-functional squads (Engineering, UX/UI Design, Data Science, and Analytics) from discovery and prototyping through launch, A/B experimentation, and iteration.
• Customer Obsession: Synthesize qualitative user research, behavioral analytics, and customer feedback to uncover friction points in the travel search, booking, or post-booking lifecycle.
• Data-Driven Optimization: Establish clear KPIs and success metrics (e.g., conversion rate, repeat booking rate, redemption volume, NPS), using experimentation and funnel analysis to prioritize high-ROI features.
• Ecosystem & Partner Management: Collaborate with third-party travel suppliers, global distribution systems (GDS), and internal card/rewards teams to integrate seamless payment, points redemption, and loyalty benefits.
• Risk & Governance: Navigate regulatory, compliance, and operational risk requirements inherent to financial services while maintaining rapid product velocity.
In this role, you’ll learn the essentials of being a product manager, and we’ll invest in you to grow in four key areas:
• Human Centered
• You’ll collaborate with tech teams to build comprehensive acceptance criteria, identifying and elevating any need for additional research to define future feature design
• You'll breakdown business epics into features and further into user stories, driving your team towards lowest effort or Minimal Viable Product (MVP) for a valid feature test
• Business Focused
• Demonstrating a growth mindset, you’ll effectively use hypothesis-driven assessment of data to ensure your product or feature delivers on real business needs
• You’ll own and prioritize feature development roadmaps, ensuring all necessary processes and procedures are followed to manage risk
• Technology Driven
• You’ll work autonomously in an agile environment, to conduct research and develop features that utilize new and evolving technology
• You’ll collaborate with designers, technologists, data scientists and subject-matter experts to build cutting edge solutions to help customers
• You’ll deliver well-managed product platforms for customers by seeking to understand technology trends and architecture strategy
• Transformational Leadership
• By actively participating in horizontal forums, you’ll harness a network of trusted relationships among tech teams, designers, key internal stakeholders and partner teams
• You’ll articulate a succinct product roadmap to deliver business value and share with with stakeholders, elevating your team’s results and becoming a product matter expert
We want you if you are:
• Intellectually Curious. You ask why, you explore, you're not afraid to blurt out your crazy idea or follow an email chain for weeks to find someone with an answer. Comfortable with ambiguity, a hunger to learn and a seeker of new challenges
• Communicator & Influencer. You can communicate complex ideas clearly regardless of your audience. Our team knows their priorities and why they’re doing what they’re doing. You always can rally associates to work with you
• Do-er. You’re biased toward action, you try things and sometimes you fail. You can get around roadblocks and stay focused on your goals. You’re well organized, able to multitask and able to prioritize your work

• You’ll deliver well-managed product platforms for customers by seeking to understand technology trends and architecture strategy
• Transformational Leadership

Manager, Product Manager, Small Business Bank
Product Management at Capital One is a booming, vibrant craft that requires reimagining the status quo, finding value creation opportunities, and driving innovative and sustainable customer experiences through technology. We believe our portfolio of businesses and investments in growth and transformation will result in a company with the scale, brand, capabilities, talent, and values to succeed as the digital revolution transforms our society and our industry.
Why Join the Small Business Bank team?
• Small businesses are the backbone of the U.S. economy. They make up 99.9% of all U.S. businesses, represent 43.5% of the country’s GDP, and employ 61 million people. Their success is critical to our collective success.
• Help us scale our national direct bank by building digital banking capabilities that directly empower these businesses to grow, scale, and thrive. You'll define, build, and accelerate the future of business banking.
• If you’ve seen Catch Me If You Can and are excited to stop fraudsters, we’ve got a perfect Product Manager position for you. You will be leading a team that uses data and cutting edge technology (e.g. AI / ML) to identify risky behaviors to keep our customers’ money safe. But any added friction makes it harder for our real customers, so it will be important to find the right balance between security and ease of use. And just when you think you’ve figured it out, the fraudsters will try something new (they are very inventive), so be ready for a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
In this role, you’ll learn the essentials of being a product manager, and we’ll invest in you to grow in four key areas:
• Human Centered
• You’ll collaborate with tech teams to build comprehensive acceptance criteria, identifying and elevating any need for additional research to define future feature design
• You'll breakdown business epics into features and further into user stories, driving your team towards lowest effort or Minimal Viable Product (MVP) for a valid feature test
• Business Focused
• Demonstrating a growth mindset, you’ll effectively use hypothesis-driven assessment of data to ensure your product or feature delivers on real business needs
• You’ll own and prioritize feature development roadmaps, ensuring all necessary processes and procedures are followed to manage risk
• Technology Driven
• You’ll work autonomously in an agile environment, to conduct research and develop features that utilize new and evolving technology
• You’ll collaborate with designers, technologists, data scientists and subject-matter experts to build cutting edge solutions to help customers
• You’ll deliver well-managed product platforms for customers by seeking to understand technology trends and architecture strategy
• Transformational Leadership
• By actively participating in horizontal forums, you’ll harness a network of trusted relationships among tech teams, designers, key internal stakeholders and partner teams
• You’ll articulate a succinct product roadmap to deliver business value and share with with stakeholders, elevating your team’s results and becoming a product matter expert
We want you if you are:
• Intellectually Curious. You ask why, you explore, you're not afraid to blurt out your crazy idea or follow an email chain for weeks to find someone with an answer. Comfortable with ambiguity, a hunger to learn and a seeker of new challenges
• Communicator & Influencer. You can communicate complex ideas clearly regardless of your audience. Our team knows their priorities and why they’re doing what they’re doing. You always can rally associates to work with you
• Do-er. You’re biased toward action, you try things and sometimes you fail. You can get around roadblocks and stay focused on your goals. You’re well organized, able to multitask and able to prioritize your work
• Passionate & Customer Focus. You care about growing others and bringing them together around what’s possible. You get a thrill from the journey of building and shipping products, and you have a desire and ability to connect with our external or internal customers to fully understand their needs
• Learner. You have an appetite to learn new things or new technologies all while exhibiting humbleness when the time comes to ask for help
• Team Player. You enjoy working with diverse people and driving the team toward a common goal. You have the ability to put the team before yourself and establish long-lasting relationships
